Whichever lands second must re-verify the line still exists in stale form before reframing (the first landing may have already rewritten it). #57 IS the convergence loop, so the read-only `plan-tool convergence` diagnostic — not the escalate_to_split bridge — is its true 'surface automatically' fulfillment; if both reframes survive, dedupe so the line points at the diagnostic.** — Two un-merged plans target the identical sentence with different replacement text; a blind second reframe either fails to match (line already changed) or layers a contradictory claim. The existing project lesson records step 9's reframe of this line as if the bridge fulfills #57, but #57's actual v1 is the diagnostic — so the two reframes can assert competing 'X is what #57 proposed' claims. _(when: when a plan-tool step reframes RUNBOOK's 'BACKLOG #57 proposes to surface automatically' re-decompose line, or reasons about which feature fulfills #57)_ _(e.g. Step 5 rewrites the re-decompose subsection's trailing parenthetical to point at the landed `plan-tool convergence` command; the captured escalate-to-split step-9 lesson reframes the same parenthetical to point at the bridge. Both cannot be the literal '#57 surfaces this automatically' answer.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **cli/completeness_cmd.py persists ONLY correctness_recs + conceptual_recs to the saved report (via save_review); the granularity advisor's smell_recs (source 'granularity-split') are DROPPED before persistence. No granularity-split source reaches the saved completeness sidecar in v1 — any cross-run reader keyed on it reads nothing until a producer change lands.** — An earlier lesson framed granularity-split as 'the live per-step signal that flows into completeness report history'; in fact the producer filters it out, so a consumer that forks on it is inert. Knowing this scopes the consumer honestly (generic frozenset[str], no granularity import). _(when: when a plan-tool step expects granularity-split (or any granularity smell_rec) to appear in saved completeness report history)_ _(e.g. Step 2 kept RegionTrend.sources a generic frozenset[str] (no GRANULARITY_SPLIT_SOURCE import) and deferred the granularity-backed localized path to a producer-change in the plan's Deferred.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **Neither plan_tool/review.py nor plan_tool/convergence.py exports a severity ORDER/RANK map — convergence.py exports only is_blocking/BLOCKING_SEVERITIES (membership). A step needing max/min/ordered severity must mint its own rank dict (e.g. _SEVERITY_RANK={'medium':1,'high':2,'critical':3}) as the single source.** — An author greps for an existing ordering constant, finds is_blocking, and assumes an order helper exists; it doesn't, so the rank must be minted locally and offered as the single source for sibling steps' render rather than re-declared. _(when: when a plan-tool step needs to order/rank severities (max_severity, sort by severity) rather than just test blocking membership)_ _(e.g. Step 2 added _SEVERITY_RANK for max_severity (grep confirmed no existing order constant) and noted step 4's render reuses it rather than re-declaring.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **review.APPLY_ELIGIBLE_SOURCES is a frozenset; review.is_apply_eligible takes a full Recommendation. To scope the lighter RunFinding model (step 1's normalized record) to apply-eligible sources, filter on `finding.source in APPLY_ELIGIBLE_SOURCES`, NOT is_apply_eligible.** — Reaching for is_apply_eligible forces constructing a Recommendation from a RunFinding (or fails the type); membership on the frozenset runs directly over the light record and single-sources the eligible set (which excludes plan-completeness). _(when: when a plan-tool step filters RunFinding (or another non-Recommendation record) to apply-eligible sources)_ _(e.g. Step 2's recurring_regions scoped findings with `source in APPLY_ELIGIBLE_SOURCES and is_blocking(severity)` over RunFinding.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **write_completeness_report→save_review persists EMPTY annotations; only the interactive completeness-apply walk populates per-rec annotations. So any signal derived from saved annotations (apply/skip/halt_reason — hence closed-state) is INERT on the mandated --iterate-only workflow: every region reads open.** — A feature keyed on annotation status looks correct in tests (which inject annotations) but is dead on the standard authoring workflow that never runs completeness-apply — a non-obvious producer-side limitation, not a consumer bug. _(when: when a plan-tool step derives a signal from saved completeness/reconcile annotations (status / halt_reason))_ _(e.g. Step 2's closed-state only ever flips on history that went through an apply-walk; on --iterate-only runs annotations are empty so closed stays False. Persisting iterate disposition as annotations is parked in the plan's Deferred.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **Reconcile report sidecars each audit a SINGLE step (snapshot.step_id set); completeness snapshots carry step_id=None. A cross-run series/window over report history must partition reconcile kinds on (kind, step_id), not kind alone — partitioning on kind alone compares findings from audits of different steps and fabricates recurrence.** — Lumping all detail-reconcile runs into one series makes two different steps' findings look like the same region recurring; including step_id keeps the window comparing audits of the same step. _(when: when a plan-tool step windows/partitions saved report history that mixes completeness and per-step reconcile sidecars)_ _(e.g. Step 2's series_key returns (kind,) for completeness and (kind, step_id) for detail-reconcile/run-reconcile; partition_series groups runs by it before matching.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **RunSnapshot fingerprint fields use sentinel/truthiness conventions a converging-certificate must honor: plan_fingerprint == '' means UNSET (matches review_persistence.SavedReview.plan_fingerprint) — an all-'' trailing streak is NOT stability evidence; code_fingerprint is a path->hash dict whose presence is truthiness (empty = not computed), so an all-empty code_fingerprint must not block a streak that plan_fingerprint alone certifies.** — A stability check that treats '' as a real fingerprint would certify 'converging' off two unset runs (false stability); one that requires a non-empty code_fingerprint would refuse to certify runs where code hashing was skipped. Both are silent misreads keyed on the sentinel meaning. _(when: when a plan-tool step reads RunSnapshot.plan_fingerprint / code_fingerprint or builds a fingerprint-stability check over report history)_ _(e.g. Step 3's _fingerprint_stable_streak skips the '' plan_fingerprint sentinel and compares code_fingerprint only among trailing runs whose code_fingerprint is non-empty (truthy), matching review_persistence's code_fingerprint_present note.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **Converged/unchanged plans in this repo persist NO new report sidecar (the reconcile-plan --refresh fingerprint gate / skip_sidecar_write path writes nothing on no-drift), so a cross-run convergence detector over saved reports CANNOT rely on a hard '>= N saved runs' floor — the most-converged plans stop accruing history. The converging verdict needs a below-floor escape hatch.** — An author assuming history grows monotonically while a plan is worked will build a >=N-runs gate that the done plans can never satisfy (they stopped generating sidecars), freezing them at insufficient-history. This is a producer-side quirk invisible from the consumer's type. _(when: when a plan-tool step builds a detector/metric over saved completeness/reconcile report history and gates on a minimum saved-run count)_ _(e.g. Step 3 added the fingerprint-stable below-window converging path specifically because skip_sidecar_write means a converged plan persists no sidecar and converged plans stop accruing history.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **The committed tests/fixtures/convergence/sample-report-history.json is ONE already-normalized JSON file (a list of run dicts), NOT a tree of real SavedReview sidecars in a reports/ dir. Test strategy splits accordingly: model-SHAPE tests (ReportHistory/RunSnapshot/RunFinding fields, and step 2's detector cases that mutate the payload inline for converging/short variants) load this fixture directly; tests exercising load_report_history's DISK-reading path instead write real sidecars via review_persistence.save_review into a tmp_path reports dir. Don't author a new fixture or stand up a fake reports tree for model tests.** — A normalized single-file fixture lets model and detector tests build the records without faking review_persistence's directory layout, while the save_review-into-tmp_path path is the only honest way to exercise the real glob/parse/kind-filter/ordering reader. An author who confuses the two either stands up an unnecessary fake reports tree for a model assertion or asserts the reader works by loading the pre-normalized fixture (which bypasses load_report_history entirely). _(when: when a plan-tool step authors or consumes the convergence fixture, or tests a reader over saved completeness/reconcile report sidecars)_ _(e.g. Step 1: test_fixture_loads_into_model deserializes sample-report-history.json into the 3-run spinning shape; test_load_report_history_reads_saved_sidecars / _runs_sorted_oldest_to_newest / _kind_filter_* write real completeness/reconcile/review sidecars with save_review into tmp_path and assert the reader's flattening, ordering, and kind-filtering.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/completeness_report.py:_blocked_next_step (with _blocked_split_targets resolving the (step_id, title) pairs) is the single source for the repo's split-recommendation command shape: `plan-tool split <plan_name> --step <sid> --into "<first sub-step>" --into "<second sub-step>"` with the two `--into` titles left as placeholders for BLOCKED apply findings. Any new code recommending a step split must mirror this exact shape and placeholder convention; the structural-re-decompose alternative is `plan-tool create <slug> --from-existing <seed.md>` (template only, no seed authored, zero Claude) mirroring RUNBOOK's re-decompose workflow.** — An author emitting a new split recommendation who invents a different flag order or placeholder style gives operators two inconsistent recipes for the same action. Knowing _blocked_next_step is the source-of-truth shape (and that the structural fallback is the create --from-existing template) keeps a new emitter byte-consistent and scopes consolidation to a deferred reconcile refactor. _(when: when a plan-tool step renders a `plan-tool split` (or structural re-decompose `create --from-existing`) recommendation command)_ _(e.g. Step 4's _split_command copied completeness_report.py:_blocked_next_step's recipe verbatim; _reseed_command emitted `plan-tool create <slug> --from-existing <seed.md>`; folding the two split builders onto one shared function was deferred to reconcile.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **The landed `plan-tool convergence` command is modeled on `plan_tool/cli/inspect.py:cmd_status` — args-only, always `return 0` for EVERY verdict (no-history / insufficient-history / converging / spinning), and builds ONLY a `-y/--yes` parent. This SUPERSEDES the earlier captured step-4 lesson (from the prior plan decomposition) that described cmd_convergence building a `fail_on_findings_parent` and returning rc 1 on 'spinning' — the re-decomposed plan's step-5 title (`no --fail-on-findings/--min-runs`) reversed that. A future reconcile/docs pass must NOT regress to adding a fail-on-findings rc-flip to this command.** — Two captured project lessons now describe the same handler with opposite exit-code policies; a reconcile reading the older step-4 bullet would re-add a fail_on_findings_parent and break the deliberate always-exit-0 contract. - `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/cli/gitcommit.py is the repo's stdlib-only git-subprocess LEAF — every git wrapper here runs `subprocess.run([...], cwd=repo_root, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True, text=True)`, NEVER raises on git failure, and returns `(proc.returncode, proc.stderr.strip())` for mutating verbs or a typed value / empty sentinel (`[]`, `None`, `False`) for read verbs. Any command module imports it without an import cycle. New git primitives extend this pattern in place — no consolidation, no new module.** — Future plan steps needing git calls must match this exact idiom (rc-0-is-the-only-positive, never-raise) and home them in gitcommit.py rather than forking a parallel git vocabulary; an author who raises on failure or returns a dict breaks the module's uniform caller contract. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds or reasons about a git-subprocess wrapper)_ _(e.g. Step 1 added worktree_add/list/remove/prune + clone_repo beside current_branch/branch_exists/list_branches/create_and_checkout_branch, all `(rc, tail)` or empty-on-failure; worktree_list returns `[]` on any non-zero rc, matching list_branches's posture.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **tests/cli/test_gitcommit.py drives REAL git against `tmp_path` (no claude backend) via the file's existing `_init_git_repo` / `_git` / `_commit_initial` helpers, one test class per primitive. A new git-wrapper test reuses these helpers and asserts on observable git state (current_branch(<wt>), dir existence, rc/tail), NOT subprocess mocks.** — gitcommit.py wrappers are integration-tested against a real repo, so a new primitive's tests follow suit; reaching for subprocess mocks diverges from the file's established style and misses git's real refusal behavior (same-branch-twice, dirty-remove) the wrappers exist to surface. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds tests for a gitcommit.py git wrapper)_ _(e.g. Step 1's TestWorktreeAdd/List/Remove/Prune/CloneRepo each build a real tmp_path repo with the helpers and assert real git outcomes: same-branch-twice → rc!=0 + non-empty tail; detached entry → branch=None; dirty remove refused without force then succeeds with force.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **For this repo's worktree/clone provisioning, the per-workspace branch must be BORN INSIDE the provisioning call: `git worktree add -b <branch> <path> <start_point>` (NEVER a main-tree `git switch -c` first — git refuses to add a worktree on a branch already checked out in the main tree). A CLONE is an independent repo with no co-checkout conflict, so it is TWO-PHASE: `git clone <src> <dst>` then `git -C <dst> switch -c|<branch>`. Never use `git clone -b <branch>` (it fails when the branch doesn't yet exist in the source).** — git's 'same branch can't be checked out in two worktrees' rule makes the obvious provision-then-switch sequence fail with no obvious cause; the worktree `-b` rule and the clone two-phase asymmetry (and the clone-b pitfall) are the load-bearing design constraints every later step in the Parallel Plan Worktrees plan inherits. _(when: when a plan-tool step provisions or reasons about git worktrees/clones carrying a per-workspace branch)_ _(e.g. Step 1's worktree_add uses `add -b` for create=True and `add <path> <branch>` for create=False; clone_repo clones then `git -C <clone> switch -c <branch> <start_point>` (create=True) or plain `switch <branch>` (DWIM-tracks origin), explicitly NOT `clone -b`.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/cli/run_cmd.py has its OWN `working_tree_dirty` for `run`'s `--commit` helper — deliberately separate from gitcommit.py's git wrappers (per the module docstring). Do NOT route new worktree/clone primitives through it or consolidate the two clean-tree checks.** — An author adding git primitives may try to reuse run_cmd's dirty check, but it belongs to run's commit flow; folding the two couples unrelated concerns and drags the worktree primitives into run's lifecycle. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds git primitives and considers reusing run_cmd.py's working_tree_dirty)_ _(e.g. Step 1 left run_cmd's working_tree_dirty untouched and kept worktree_remove/worktree_prune policy-free, relying on git's own dirty refusal rather than a shared dirty gate.)_
- `[cross-step]` **The Parallel Plan Worktrees plan layers cleanly: step 1 = policy-free git primitives in gitcommit.py (worktree add/list/remove/prune + clone_repo, all `(rc,tail)`/empty); step 2 = per-slug path derivation + `worktree_base` config in plan_tool/worktree.py; step 3 = the `worktree` command group + start_point resolution (default-branch HEAD else literal HEAD) + branch-name resolution + kind dispatch and main-tree filtering in `list`; step 4 = destructive remove/prune with clean-tree pre-gate + confirmation. The step-1 primitives consume an ALREADY-RESOLVED branch/start_point and add no gating.** — Later steps (2–4) need the boundaries to avoid re-deriving: the primitives take path/branch/start_point as givens and own no policy, so step 3 owns all resolution and step 4 owns all gates. An author wiring a later step must not push resolution or gating back down into the primitives. _(when: when a plan-tool step touches the Parallel Plan Worktrees plan's gitcommit primitives, worktree.py, or the worktree command group)_ _(e.g. Step 1's Deferred assigned path/config to step 2, start_point + branch resolution + kind dispatch to step 3, and the clean-tree gate/confirmation to step 4, keeping worktree_list returning every porcelain block unfiltered.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/project_config.py is the repo's TOLERANT layered-config reader: project (.plan-tool/config.json via project_config_path(repo_root)) → user (~/.plan-tool/config.json via user_config_path()) → default, with private per-level readers (_read_level, _read_smell_block) that NEVER raise (absent/bad-JSON/non-dict/missing-key/wrong-type → 'level unset'), warn-once to stderr on a present-but-invalid value, and have NO env axis for repo/user settings (branch_prefixes/validation_machinery_paths). user_config_path() evaluates Path.home() IN-BODY so tests patch $HOME per case. Picking the wrong module's posture either crashes on a broken lower-priority file or swallows a malformed authoritative one. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds/reads a config key or chooses between tolerant and strict config-reader posture)_ _(e.g. Step 2's plan_tool/worktree.py reused project_config_path/user_config_path, added a third tolerant reader _read_worktree_base (keyed on 'worktree_base') mirroring _read_level/_read_smell_block, used no env axis (matching branch_prefixes), and patched Path.home() in user-level tests.)_

Everything else in the new-subcommand fan-out (app `cmd_<name>` re-import for test_package_surface, parser order, cli_reference --write, golden re-baseline with UPDATE_CLI_GOLDEN=1) is identical to the single-command recipe.** — The captured single-command recipe (cmd_convergence) doesn't cover the group shape; an author may try to register cmd_add/cmd_list separately or expect them on the package surface and red test_package_surface. runs.py is the in-repo template; only one cmd_<group> is registered and surfaced. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a CLI command GROUP with multiple verbs/subactions)_ _(e.g. Step 3 wired `worktree`: worktree_cmd.py (cmd_worktree + register returning {'worktree': cmd_worktree}, add/list internal) + app.py dual import + COMMAND_MODULES append + parser.py CANONICAL_COMMAND_ORDER after 'detach-branch' + __init__ Workspaces catalog block + 'cmd_worktree' in __all__ + cli_reference --write + golden re-baseline.)_
- `[cross-step]` **In the Parallel Plan Worktrees plan, step 3's worktree_cmd.py owns ALL resolution the step-1 primitives and step-2 pure leaf left out: `_resolve_branch` precedence = explicit `--branch` > `derive_branch(slug, branch_prefixes(repo))` when `branch_awareness_enabled(repo)` else the bare slug (branch-awareness OFF, the project default, maps to the slug — matching derive_worktree_path's slug segment); `_resolve_start_point` = `default_branch(repo) or 'HEAD'`; `create = not branch_exists(repo, branch)` selects `-b` (born off start_point) vs plain checkout. - `[domain-shape]` **`worktree list` builds `wt_by_path = {Path(e.path).resolve(): e for e in worktree_list(repo_root)}` and MUST drop the entry whose resolved path == `repo_root.resolve()` — git `worktree --porcelain` always lists the main working tree as the first block, and `list` reports plan WORKSPACES, not the repo. Kind dispatch per registered plan: target.resolve() in wt_by_path → kind `worktree` (branch from WorktreeEntry.branch, refs/heads-stripped, None when detached); else `(target/'.git').is_dir()` → kind `clone` (branch from current_branch(target)); else skip. Dirty from gitcommit.working_tree_dirty(target), NOT run_cmd's separate working_tree_dirty (that belongs to run's --commit helper). Always returns 0, no Claude, no mutation.** — Step 1 deliberately left worktree_list returning every porcelain block unfiltered, deferring the main-tree filter to step 3; this records the exact filter and the kind-dispatch/dirty-probe shape so the deferral closes correctly and a reuse of run_cmd's dirty check (which would couple the worktree group to run's commit lifecycle) is avoided. _(when: when a plan-tool step implements or edits worktree list / kind dispatch / workspace dirty reporting)_ _(e.g. Step 3's _classify_workspace_kind + _cmd_worktree_list iterate ctx.entries, derive target via derive_worktree_path(repo, slug), skip ABSENT targets, exclude the main tree from wt_by_path, and report slug/kind/branch/path/dirty per workspace with a 'no workspaces' line + rc 0 when empty.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **In the Parallel Plan Worktrees teardown, the two workspace KINDS delete via different engines with opposite safety postures: a `worktree` is removed by gitcommit.worktree_remove (`git worktree remove [--force]`, which natively refuses a dirty tree) while a `clone` is removed by `shutil.rmtree` (no git involvement, deletes unconditionally). So the command-layer `_dirty_gate` (working_tree_dirty(target) and not force → refuse) is the ONLY protection for a dirty clone, and `--force` is what lets rmtree proceed on it. Reuse gitcommit.working_tree_dirty for the gate — never run_cmd.py's separate working_tree_dirty (that belongs to run's --commit helper).** — An author who relies on git's dirty refusal will leave the clone path unprotected, since rmtree never refuses; the command-layer gate must run uniformly before kind dispatch. Reusing run_cmd's dirty check would couple the worktree group to run's commit lifecycle (a non-consolidation recorded since step 1). _(when: when a plan-tool step removes or reasons about deleting a worktree-vs-clone workspace and its dirty/clean-tree gate)_ _(e.g. Step 4: `_dirty_gate(target, force=args.force)` runs before `_classify_workspace_kind` dispatch; worktree → worktree_remove(repo, target, force), clone → shutil.rmtree(target) in try/except OSError; `test_remove_clone_dirty_refused_without_force` proves the command-layer gate is the clone's only guard.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **`worktree prune` discovers dead candidates statelessly: `base = worktree_base(repo).resolve()`, `registered = {derive_worktree_path(repo, slug_from_filename(e.path)).resolve() for e in ctx.entries}`, then each worktree_list entry under `base` but NOT in `registered` is a dead candidate. It also calls gitcommit.worktree_prune (git admin GC) for path-gone worktrees. Because a CLONE has no git-worktree registry entry, worktree_list never reports it — so prune covers deregistered WORKTREES only; a deregistered clone is undiscoverable (slug gone from manifest, no registry entry) and is a documented manual-cleanup limitation. No per-workspace registry is added (no-extra-state tenet).** — An author may assume prune sweeps all plan-tool workspaces; it can only see what worktree_list reports, scoped to worktree_base. Knowing the discovery shape (base scope + registered-set subtraction + git admin GC) and the clone blind-spot keeps the verb correct and the limitation explicit rather than a silent orphan-leak. _(when: when a plan-tool step implements or reasons about worktree prune / dead-workspace discovery in worktree_cmd.py)_ _(e.g. Step 4's `_cmd_worktree_prune` builds registered from ctx.entries, treats under-base-but-unregistered worktree_list entries as dead, runs worktree_prune for path-gone admin, applies the dirty-surface rule per surviving candidate, then worktree_remove(..., force=False) the clean ones after one batch confirm.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **The destructive `_confirm(prompt, *, yes)` idiom for a plan-tool command is modeled EXACTLY on plan_tool/cli/manifest.py:_prompt_remove_missing (not imported — minted locally per module): yes True → return True (no prompt); not sys.stdin.isatty() and not yes → print a `re-run with -y` hint to stderr and return False (an unattended run never silently deletes); interactive TTY → builtins.input(f"{prompt} [y/N]: ") returning True only on y/yes, with EOFError/KeyboardInterrupt caught → print 'cancelled' → return False. The `-y/--yes` parent is likewise built locally (manifest.py / checkpoints.py / bench_cmd.py each mint their own).** — A destructive plan-tool verb must inherit the repo's never-delete-unattended guarantee; copying manifest.py's exact branch shape (TTY vs non-TTY vs explicit yes, EOF handling) keeps the confirmation UX consistent across commands and the non-TTY hint honest. Reaching for a shared import fails — there is no shared confirm helper; consolidation is a standing deferred reconcile item. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a destructive verb needing a TTY confirmation prompt or a local -y/--yes parent)_ _(e.g. Step 4's `_confirm` mirrors _prompt_remove_missing and is reused by both `remove` (per-target) and `prune` (per-batch); tests cover TTY-decline keeps workspace, non-TTY-without-yes declines + hint, and -y bypasses input.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **The plan-tool 'document a new operator feature' surface set is six files with a fixed fidelity tier: README.md + RUNBOOK.md carry the FULL workflow/caveats, CLAUDE.md gets ONE `## Architecture` paragraph (summary), BACKLOG.md gets any forward-looking deferred-convenience entry, and integrations/claude/SKILL.md + integrations/codex/SKILL.md are near-identical ROUTERS (a `## Subcommands at a glance` row + a `## Decision tree for common user asks` row, pointer-only, edited in lockstep). docs/cli/<name>.md is GENERATED — not part of this set.** — A future docs step that lands a feature can copy this exact surface map and tiering instead of rediscovering which doc owns what depth; missing the SKILL-pair lockstep or restating full caveats in a router are the recurring mistakes. _(when: when a plan-tool docs step must describe a newly-shipped operator command/feature across README/RUNBOOK/CLAUDE/BACKLOG/SKILL)_ _(e.g. Step 5 documented the worktree group: full in README+RUNBOOK, one CLAUDE Architecture paragraph, one BACKLOG `### A` entry for the deferred `--worktree` convenience, identical Workspaces rows in both SKILL files, and explicitly left docs/cli/worktree.md to steps 3/4's cli_reference --write.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **convergence_diagnosis.py's fork vocabulary is a set of `FORK_*` string constants (FORK_LOCALIZED / FORK_STRUCTURAL / FORK_NONE, plus FORK_SCOPE_OUT) that `classify_fork` emits and that `_spinning_body`/`render_diagnosis` and the `plan-tool convergence` CLI key on by literal — the constants' docstring says 'do not inline the literals downstream.' classify_fork's single-resolved-step arm (`None not in foci and len(resolved) == 1`) is the ONLY place a per-step sub-fork (localized / scope-out) can live — there every recurring region is co-located on one step; distinct-step, multi-region, or unresolvable evidence falls to FORK_STRUCTURAL. A new per-step remedy branches inside that arm; it must NOT touch the structural branch.** — A step adding a new remedy may either hardcode the fork literal downstream (breaking the single-source convention) or try to fire a per-step remedy on multi-step evidence; the single-resolved-step arm is the correctness boundary that guarantees one resolved step exists to act on. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a new fork state or per-step sub-arm to convergence_diagnosis.py:classify_fork / _spinning_body)_ _(e.g. Step 1 added FORK_SCOPE_OUT beside the existing three, branched inside the `len(resolved)==1` arm via `any(_region_triggers_scope_out(r) for r in regions)`, left the structural branch (FORK_STRUCTURAL + _reseed_command + ambiguous flag) untouched, and added a third explicit branch to _spinning_body's fork dispatch.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/review.py CANNOT import from plan_tool/granularity.py — granularity.py:30 does `from plan_tool.review import Invoker, Recommendation, _make_rec_id`, so the reverse edge would cycle. - `[review-heuristic]` **To add a NON-apply-eligible advisory finding to review.py that rides the neutral generic triage branch: leave its source out of BOTH STRUCTURAL_SOURCES and APPLY_ELIGIBLE_SOURCES (that is what makes is_structural() and is_apply_eligible() return False, so triage_reason hits the `if not is_apply_eligible(rec)` generic branch). The canonical verdict→resolution mapping is: APPLIED → (CARRIED_RESOLUTION_APPLIED, ""); BLOCKED / BLOCKED-STRUCTURAL → (CARRIED_RESOLUTION_BLOCKED, verdict) [the reason carries the raw verdict so STRUCTURAL stays distinguishable]; everything else (NOT-APPLICABLE, UNKNOWN) → (CARRIED_RESOLUTION_SKIPPED, verdict). This mapping is currently local (_resolution_for_verdict in completeness_phases.py); if create/reconcile later need it, consolidate via reconcile, don't duplicate.** — An author wiring a new apply-verdict consumer needs the exact verdict set and its resolution mapping (notably that BLOCKED-STRUCTURAL also maps to blocked and both keep the verdict as reason); guessing the vocabulary mis-buckets a verdict and loses the structural distinction. The checkpoint ordering is load-bearing: save_checkpoint belongs in the prefix right after a successful parse, but discard_checkpoint MUST stay in the serial tail AFTER update_step_detail_field — the durability hedge requires the checkpoint to outlive the plan-pointer write.** — An author splitting this loop for concurrency who moves discard_checkpoint into the worker breaks the 'claude succeeded but the plan pointer isn't set yet' hedge; knowing the exact prefix/tail boundary and the discard-after-plan-write rule keeps the split behavior-preserving. _(when: when a plan-tool step extracts/reorders generate_detail's per-step loop or touches its save_checkpoint/discard_checkpoint ordering)_ _(e.g. Step 1 put save_checkpoint in the worker and explicitly kept discard_checkpoint after update_step_detail_field, treating the prefix/tail cut as 'does this mutate the plan file or depend on cross-step ordered state?'.)_

The in-loop-vs-post-loop distinction is the correctness boundary. _(when: when a plan-tool step parallelizes generate_detail or reasons about its two escalate_to_split call sites under --iterate)_ _(e.g. Step 2's guard rejects jobs>1 + budget.enabled and leaves the post-loop mixed_steps escalate pass untouched.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **`granularity-split` has exactly FOUR producers, a closed world: three DETERMINISTIC detectors — `_title_mixes_refactor_and_feature`→"mixed-verbs", `_title_conjoins_clauses`→"two-clauses", `_step_spans_unrelated_areas`→"multi-area" (each feeding `_split_rec` with fingerprint `f"split:{key}:{step.id}"`) — plus the PROSE kernel `parse_mixed_step_findings` (no predicate key in its fingerprint; id keyed on free-form desc). Severity discriminates the two kinds: deterministic recs are `severity="info"`, prose recs `severity="medium"` (via `_GRANULARITY_SEV`). Because the set is closed, a `granularity-split` rec matching no deterministic key IS the prose mixed-step kind.** — An author wiring telemetry or recovery over granularity-split findings must know there are four producers (not three), that only three carry a structured predicate key, and that severity (info vs medium) is the exact secondary discriminator for the prose kernel — guessing the producer set mis-partitions the recovery or drops the prose case. _(when: when a plan-tool step reads, counts, or recovers granularity-split predicate keys, or reasons about which granularity-split findings carry a machine key)_ _(e.g. Step 1 added SPLIT_PREDICATE_* constants for the three deterministic keys plus mixed-step for the prose kernel, exported the key set as the single source both detectors and the recovery helper read, and classified the prose rec by closed-world/severity fallback.)_

Do NOT add a predicate-key field to the frozen `review.Recommendation` to carry the key — keep it in granularity.py's constants + recovery helper (preserves the granularity→review one-way leaf edge).** — Both id stability and the cycle-free leaf posture constrain how a machine key can be exposed: changing a literal moves every rec id (test_ids_are_stable fails), and widening Recommendation drags a schema change into review.py that the granularity leaf must not require. The re-derivation helper stays inside granularity.py because it already imports _make_rec_id and owns the fingerprint shape. _(when: when a plan-tool step exposes or recovers a machine key off a granularity/review Recommendation, or considers changing a granularity predicate literal or adding a field to review.Recommendation)_ _(e.g. Step 1's split_predicate_key(rec) re-derives against the id format using the already-imported _make_rec_id, leaves review.Recommendation unchanged, and keeps test_ids_are_stable green.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/create.py:_review_step_change_types's interactive `while` loop is the ONLY create-stage per-step operator-gesture loop. _ask_change_type returns one of three shapes: the _SPLIT sentinel, a concrete ChangeType, or None (Enter on an unproposed step). Classify the action by value comparison against step.change_type (no need to widen _ask_change_type). had_split_hint reads off the per-iteration hint_map (bool(hint_map.get(step.id))); the split branch records split-requested before _propose_step_split and a terminal after, with step_id = str(pre-split step.id) and before_steps captured before reviewed = _apply_step_split reassigns. The only other split actuators (detail.py:escalate_to_split, cli/review_actions.py structural arm) are different paths, out of scope.** — An author wiring per-step outcome telemetry needs the exact return vocabulary of _ask_change_type, the value-comparison classification, the hint_map source for had_split_hint, and the pre-split-id / pre-reassignment count rules — guessing any of these mis-records the action or the counts, and reaching for the detail/review split actuators wires the wrong loop. _(when: when a plan-tool step records or reasons about per-step operator gestures in create.py's _review_step_change_types interactive loop)_ _(e.g. Step 4 added _record_step_outcome called per branch: accept/override/unclassified-accepted before reviewed[i]=...; split-requested right after `if answer is _SPLIT:`; split-applied (before_steps/after_steps/proposal_len=len(replacements)=2) / split-unusable (replacements is None) / split-invalid (error_class='CreateError', no message) in their existing arms before each continue.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **create.py's change-type review has TWO telemetry altitudes with OPPOSITE mode discipline: the per-PASS assessment (step 3, decision='create-review') is recorded at all FOUR return branches WITH a CREATE_MODE_* constant; the per-STEP outcome (step 4, decision='create-step-outcome') carries NO mode and is recorded ONLY inside the interactive loop — because --yes, non-TTY, and checkpoint-resume return before the loop and present no per-step gesture, so a per-step outcome there would be meaningless.** — An author who saw the step-3 four-site/mode-tagged pattern may reflexively add a mode to the outcome event or try to emit it in the non-interactive branches; the outcome is inherently interactive and the non-interactive branches have no gesture, so mode is redundant and those branches must stay outcome-free (the step-3 assessment already counts them). _(when: when a plan-tool step adds per-step vs per-pass telemetry in create.py's change-type review and must decide whether a mode tag and the non-interactive branches apply)_ _(e.g. Step 4's outcome event omits mode entirely and is emitted only in the interactive while loop; the --yes/non-TTY/checkpoint accept-verbatim paths emit no create-step-outcome line (deferred-by-design, covered by step 3's assessment).)_

- `[domain-shape]` **DATA_CONTRACT.md's drift guard has two distinct lanes: tests/test_data_contract.py:test_every_persisted_field_is_documented introspects DATACLASS FIELDS (e.g. DecisionEvent's declared attributes) — it is blind to keys inside the open DecisionEvent.context bag — while the per-vocabulary doc-presence tests (test_report_kinds_documented, test_schema_version_named) are substring scans over _doc_text(). A step adding new context keys/decision values under an existing event family must extend the SUBSTRING-scan lane (a sibling test beside test_report_kinds_documented), never expect the field lane to catch it; and document the keys in a per-decision context-key table below the DecisionEvent field table, since the open bag can't be expressed as field rows.** — An author who sees test_every_persisted_field_is_documented assumes any new persisted key is drift-guarded; but context keys are values in an untyped dict, so that test stays green while the doc lags. Knowing the two lanes (field-introspection vs substring-presence) routes the new guard to the only one that can catch a missing context key. _(when: when a plan-tool step documents new keys/values in the DecisionEvent context bag (or any open bag) in DATA_CONTRACT.md and reasons about which test_data_contract.py guard catches it)_ _(e.g. Step 5 documented create-review / create-step-outcome decision values and their context keys (mode, predicate_counts, split_step_ids, can_split, action, had_split_hint, before_steps/after_steps/proposal_len/error_class) under kind="granularity" with no DecisionEvent field change, added test_create_decisions_documented + test_create_context_keys_documented as _doc_text() substring scans, and left test_every_persisted_field_is_documented[DecisionEvent] / test_schema_version_named green.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **In plan_tool/telemetry.py, deciding whether a new recorder mints a NEW top-level kind= or reuses an existing kind= with a new decision value turns on decision-FAMILY identity, not on copying the nearest sibling: the create-stage recorders reuse kind="granularity" because create-review/create-step-outcome are the granularity family observed at a new stage, but a genuinely distinct family (a per-plan split-criteria breakdown, unrelated to granularity/audit-coverage/convergence) mints a new kind constant (PLAN_CRITERIA_BREAKDOWN_KIND="plan-criteria-breakdown"). Either way: no TELEMETRY_SCHEMA_VERSION bump (event shape unchanged), export the kind literal as a module constant other steps key on, and derive counts inside the recorder.** — The captured sibling-recorder lesson only spells out the reuse-a-kind case (create-review under granularity), so an author reflexively reuses the closest kind and buries an unrelated decision family inside it — losing the ability to filter that family by kind. The discriminator is whether the new decision belongs to an existing family's semantics, not whether a nearby recorder exists to copy. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a telemetry recorder to plan_tool/telemetry.py and must choose between reusing an existing kind= with a new decision value vs minting a new top-level kind)_ _(e.g. Step 1 minted kind="plan-criteria-breakdown" (decision="evaluated") as a new top-level family beside record_convergence/record_create_granularity_assessment — NOT a new granularity decision — because a per-criterion, fingerprint-tagged plan evaluation is not the granularity/audit-coverage/convergence family; the kind string is the contract steps 3-4 key on, the decision string is free.)_

- `[cross-step]` **When a plan-tool step builds a declarative catalog whose entries carry a stable `id` that a LATER step's evaluator maps detector output back to, the ids must REUSE the existing slugs from the owning modules — never mint fresh ones — so the mapping lines up with no translation table. Pin the reuse with a test asserting the catalog ids EQUAL the imported source slugs.** — An author coining new catalog ids forces step 3's evaluator to maintain a hand-built id↔detector map that silently drifts; reusing the live slugs (and a test that equates them to the imports) makes the mapping identity-based and self-checking. _(when: when a plan-tool step defines a catalog/registry id field that a downstream step's evaluator will map runtime detector/fork output back onto)_ _(e.g. Step 2's SPLIT_CRITERIA ids reuse granularity.SPLIT_PREDICATE_MIXED_VERBS/_CONJOINED_CLAUSES/_UNRELATED_AREAS and convergence_diagnosis.FORK_LOCALIZED/_SCOPE_OUT/_STRUCTURAL; test_catalog_reuses_granularity_predicate_slugs asserts the altitude-2 ids equal those imported constants so step 3's detector→id mapping needs no lookup table.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **convergence_diagnosis exposes a fixed reuse chain for a single plan: load_report_history(plan_path) → diagnose_convergence(history) → classify_fork(diagnosis). A consumer reuses it verbatim (writes no new spin detection): the fork arm names the criterion (FORK_LOCALIZED/FORK_SCOPE_OUT/FORK_STRUCTURAL), 'fired' = verdict is VERDICT_SPINNING AND fork is not the no-op arm, ForkRecommendation.step_focus gives the step ids, and no-history / insufficient-history must be treated as not-fired, never raised.** — An author reusing convergence detection needs the exact three-function chain and the fired/step-ids/no-history rules; guessing them re-implements spin detection or crashes on the common empty-history case. _(when: when a plan-tool step reuses convergence_diagnosis to evaluate a single plan's spin/fork state)_ _(e.g. Step 3's evaluator chains those three functions for altitude 3, keys fired off VERDICT_SPINNING + non-no-op fork, reads step ids from step_focus, and marks altitude-3 criteria not-fired when history is empty.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan-tool's split-criteria feature decomposes into THREE altitudes, each owned by a distinct leaf module the per-plan evaluator orchestrates and maps onto the step-2 catalog ids: altitude 1 (plan-too-big) = distill_thresholds.py (DISTILL_SKIP_BELOW_BYTES=16384 / DISTILL_ADVISE_ABOVE_BYTES=262144, data-backed + a Claude-judged split decision rendered as UNPINNED prose); altitude 2 (create-time granularity) = granularity.assess_granularity(stage='create', invoker=None, evidence=GranularityEvidence()), partitioned by GRANULARITY_SPLIT_SOURCE (→ split_predicate_key) / GRANULARITY_MERGE_SOURCE; altitude 3 (post-review spin) = the convergence_diagnosis fork chain.** — A future step touching the split-criteria evaluator or its catalog needs the altitude→module map to know which detector produces each criterion and which parts are data-backed vs Claude-judged; conflating the altitudes or re-typing the thresholds breaks the mapping and the drift-guard. _(when: when a plan-tool step edits the split-criteria evaluator/catalog or reasons about which module owns a given split criterion)_ _(e.g. Step 3's evaluate_split_criteria orchestrates exactly these three modules with invoker=None for altitude 2, compares plan_path.stat().st_size / len(plan.steps) against the imported DISTILL_* constants for altitude 1, and imports only leaves below split_criteria.py (granularity, convergence_diagnosis, review_persistence, telemetry, distill_thresholds, schema, style).)_

- `[domain-shape]` **Adding a new CLI subcommand to plan-tool touches a FIXED set of wiring sites beyond the new command module + its tests: (1) plan_tool/cli/parser.py — append the primary name to CANONICAL_COMMAND_ORDER; (2) plan_tool/cli/app.py — the module import + a `from ...<cmd> import cmd_X` re-import + appending the module to COMMAND_MODULES; (3) plan_tool/cli/__init__.py — the docstring catalog help line + the `cmd_X` __all__ entry; (4) CAPABILITIES.md surfaces. create scoped exactly this set correctly for step 4 — treat it as the canonical new-command footprint.** — An author under-scoping a new-command step drops one of these and ships a command that mis-sorts in --help, fails __all__ resolution, or trips the orphan-subcommand validate gate; the set is stable across command modules. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a new CLI subcommand module)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/capability_catalog.py:check_capabilities emits an `orphan-subcommand` finding (failing `plan-tool validate`) for any primary subcommand name that no capability lists in `surfaces`. A new subcommand must add BOTH the subcommand name AND its owning module path to one existing capability's surfaces — never a new capability block for a single read-only surface.** — Wiring the parser/app is not enough — validate cross-checks every primary name against the capability catalog, and both the command name and the module path are checked. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a new primary subcommand and must keep `plan-tool validate` green)_ _(e.g. Step 4 adds split-criteria + plan_tool/split_criteria.py to structural-remedies (which owns the split/merge/scope-out verbs); plan-completeness (owner of convergence + convergence_diagnosis.py) is the alternative home.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/cli/convergence_cmd.py is the canonical template for a read-only plan-tool diagnostic subcommand: docstring stating no-Claude / no-mutation / no-run-log / always-exit-0, a `cmd_X(args) -> int`, and a `register(subparsers) -> dict[str, Handler]` one-entry map. It imports only cycle-free leaves (cli.context, cli.parser, the domain module, locator) and never plan_tool.cli.app; its `-y/--yes` parent is inert (no confirm) and can be dropped.** — Modeling on convergence_cmd inherits the import-light posture, the always-exit-0 convention, and the register/handler seam — guessing risks importing app (cycle) or wiring an rc-flip. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a read-only (no-Claude, no-mutation) diagnostic subcommand)_
- `[detail-authoring]` **A plan-tool CLI handler that forks on an OPTIONAL positional (`nargs='?', default=None`) must guard the plan-resolution path behind `args.name is not None` — resolve_plan_for_context requires a name and errors on None, so a plan-independent mode must return before any _load_context/resolve call.** — A two-mode diagnostic (global legend vs per-plan breakdown) shares one handler; calling resolution in the no-arg mode raises where the operator expected plan-free output. _(when: when a plan-tool CLI handler branches on an optional positional between a plan-independent and a per-plan mode)_ _(e.g. cmd_split_criteria: no-arg → render_split_criteria() + return 0 (no context load); with-arg → _load_context + resolve_plan_for_context + evaluate_split_criteria.)_
- `[cross-step]` **Read-only plan-tool diagnostics (convergence, status, now split-criteria) are deliberately NOT listed in the SKILL routers (integrations/claude|codex/SKILL.md) or USE_CASES/README narrative — a new diagnostic follows that precedent and defers those surfaces rather than scoping them into the wiring step.** — The wiring step's footprint is the parser/app/__init__/capabilities/generated-reference set; pulling SKILL/USE_CASES prose in over-scopes it, and low-traffic read-only diagnostics aren't advertised there by convention. _(when: when a plan-tool step wires a read-only diagnostic subcommand and must decide whether SKILL/USE_CASES/README prose is in scope)_

- `[domain-shape]` **The two SKILL routers integrations/claude/SKILL.md and integrations/codex/SKILL.md share a `## Decision tree for common user asks` table and a `## Subcommands at a glance` table that must stay byte-identical except for the pre-existing backend-specific lines (claude vs `codex exec`). Any row added for a backend-neutral command must be added to BOTH, and the sync is verifiable: `diff integrations/claude/SKILL.md integrations/codex/SKILL.md` should surface only the known backend differences.** — A row added to one router but not the other, or worded differently, silently desyncs the agent routing between backends; the diff-parity check is the cheap contract that catches it. _(when: when a plan-tool step edits the Decision tree or Subcommands-at-a-glance tables in either integrations/*/SKILL.md)_ _(e.g. Step 5's split-criteria decision-tree row and Discovery-group Subcommands entry carry no backend-specific wording, so they must be identical in both files; acceptance was that the diff shows only pre-existing backend lines.)_
- `[cross-step]` **Read-only plan-tool diagnostics are NOT uniformly advertised in the SKILL routers: the peer command `convergence` is absent from the SKILL `## Subcommands at a glance` Discovery row (which lists only list/status/validate) and from the decision tree. So scoping a NEW read-only diagnostic INTO the SKILL routers breaks parity with its own peer — before adding, grep the routers for `convergence`/`status` and match the peer's treatment, or explicitly decide to back-fill the peer too rather than special-casing the new command.** — Create scoped step 5 to add split-criteria to the SKILL routers, but its closest peer convergence is deliberately not there — following create verbatim makes split-criteria the lone advertised read-only diagnostic, an inconsistency an operator/agent reads as an accident. _(when: when a plan-tool docs step is scoped to add a read-only diagnostic (convergence/status/scope-out family) to integrations/*/SKILL.md, USE_CASES.md, or README narrative)_ _(e.g. Step 5's detail added split-criteria to the claude/codex SKILL Discovery row and decision tree; the same body confirms convergence is not in that row (only list/status/validate), so the new command diverges from its peer's convention.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **To read a plan's per-step detail bodies from a cycle-free leaf, RE-DERIVE the bundle path locally — `plan_path.parent / "plan-details" / <plan-slug> / f"{step.id:02d}-*.md"`, first glob match, keyed by step.id — mirroring review_persistence.compute_plan_fingerprint, rather than importing plan_tool/detail.py:derive_detail_path (which would pull a heavy orchestrator into the leaf). A missing detail file contributes nothing (empty bodies → no findings).** — split_criteria.py must stay a leaf below the orchestrators; derive_detail_path lives in detail.py, so importing it for a path helper would create the exact orchestrator edge the leaf posture forbids. compute_plan_fingerprint already re-derives the same path for the same reason — reuse that convention. _(when: when a plan-tool leaf module needs to locate/read per-step detail files and is tempted to import detail.py)_ _(e.g. Step 3's altitude-2 evidence builder reads bodies: dict[int,str] by re-deriving the bundle path the way compute_plan_fingerprint does, explicitly NOT importing detail.derive_detail_path.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **For the per-plan split-criteria evaluator, call assess_granularity with stage="detail" and evidence=GranularityEvidence(detail_bodies=…), NOT stage="create": at stage="detail" the advisor also lifts the prose MIXED-STEP findings from detail bodies via parse_mixed_step_findings (a regex parse, no Claude), so `mixed-step` becomes a DETERMINISTIC criterion (fires when a recorded finding exists). The ONLY altitude-1..3 criterion left un-evaluated in the no-Claude breakdown is the altitude-1 distill split (Claude-judged on the seed). This supersedes any earlier note that altitude 2 uses stage='create'.** — stage='create' would leave mixed-step Claude-judged and un-fired in a no-Claude per-plan run; stage='detail' + detail_bodies surfaces it deterministically from the already-recorded MIXED-STEP blocks, which is the whole point of a per-plan breakdown that spends no Claude. _(when: when a plan-tool step orchestrates granularity.assess_granularity to evaluate altitude-2 criteria for a single already-detailed plan)_ _(e.g. Step 3: assess_granularity(plan, stage="detail", evidence=GranularityEvidence(detail_bodies=bodies), invoker=None); a keyless GRANULARITY_SPLIT_SOURCE rec → mixed-step; the closed split-source world means no predicate key == the prose mixed-step kind.)_
- `[cross-step]` **When a downstream step's actual behavior contradicts a FLAG VALUE an earlier step baked into a shared catalog (e.g. deterministic=False), flag it as an explicit cross-step RECONCILE item naming both the flag and the correct value — do not silently diverge or quietly rely on the wrong flag. The split-criteria mixed-step catalog entry's `deterministic` flag must read True (step 3 lifts it deterministically), even if step 2 shipped it False.** — The catalog is the shared contract the evaluator maps onto; a stale flag from an earlier step will mislead any consumer that keys behavior off it, and the contradiction is invisible unless the downstream step surfaces it as a handoff to reconcile. _(when: when a step's implemented behavior contradicts a metadata flag/value an earlier step set in a catalog both steps share)_ _(e.g. Step 3 noted: if step 2 ships the mixed-step catalog entry deterministic=False, that flag should read True to match this behavior — reconcile against the plan Architecture when step 2 lands.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **In plan_tool/split_criteria.py, correctness-sensitive deciders (detail._split_is_safe, scope_out.compute_narrow / compute_frontmatter_hash) must be reached via BODY-LOCAL imports inside evaluate_split_criteria — a module-top import drags the orchestrator layer (detail → launcher/review/granularity) into what must stay a light leaf. This is the INVERSE of the re-derive-path-locally rule: a trivial path helper (detail-bundle path) is re-derived to avoid the import edge, but a correctness-sensitive gate is imported body-local because re-typing it would drift from what escalate_to_split / scope_out_step actually refuse.** — The two rules look contradictory until you see the discriminator — re-derive when the thing is a trivial mechanical helper and drift is harmless; import (body-local, to keep the leaf posture) when the thing is a decider whose disagreement with the actuator is a correctness bug. _(when: when a plan-tool leaf module needs a correctness-sensitive decider (gate/predicate) owned by detail.py or an orchestrator, and re-deriving vs importing must be decided)_ _(e.g. Step 4 imports detail._split_is_safe and scope_out.compute_narrow inside evaluate_split_criteria's body (mirroring cli/review_actions.py's body-local imports); acceptance pins that split_criteria.py has NO module-top import of plan_tool.detail or plan_tool.scope_out.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **Split-safety in plan-tool is TWO independent per-step run-state signals, not one: split-safe = detail._split_is_safe(plan, step.id) (blocks when ANY step with id >= target is non-PENDING — a renumber would orphan its id-keyed run state); scope-out-blocked = bool(scope_out.compute_narrow(...).blockers), whose NarrowBlocker.kind set is {downstream-orphan (non-PENDING strictly AFTER the carved step), inbound-dependent (a step depends_on the carved step), non-canonical-numbering, step-missing, empty-plan}. They check different graph conditions and can disagree (split-safe=True while scope-out-blocked=True). compute_narrow is pure/read-only (only fs touch is testing a detail file's existence), safe to call from a diagnostic.** — An author reasoning about split/scope-out availability needs the exact, different blocking conditions of the two actuators — collapsing them into one 'splittable?' bit hides which structural remedy is actually open, and guessing compute_narrow mutates would wrongly bar it from a read-only surface. _(when: when a plan-tool step reasons about, reports, or gates on whether a step can be re-split or scoped-out)_ _(e.g. Step 4: split-safe reads _split_is_safe's (safe, blocking_ids); scope-out-blocked reads compute_narrow(plan, carved_id=…, plan_path=…, repo_root=…, source_frontmatter_hash=compute_frontmatter_hash(plan_path)).blockers; test_split_safe_and_scope_out_are_independent pins the disagreement.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **compute_narrow needs repo_root AND a source_frontmatter_hash (scope_out.compute_frontmatter_hash(plan_path)); the per-plan split-criteria evaluator therefore takes repo_root (added in step 4 on top of step 3's (plan, *, plan_path)) and must compute the frontmatter hash ONCE outside the per-step loop before calling compute_narrow once per step — the loop is O(N^2) over steps but plans are small (<~20), so it is acceptable.** — An author extending the evaluator will otherwise recompute the frontmatter hash per step or omit repo_root and hit compute_narrow's required args; the hoist-once + O(N^2)-is-fine note is the settled shape. _(when: when a plan-tool step calls scope_out.compute_narrow from an evaluator/diagnostic over every step of a plan)_ _(e.g. Step 4 extended evaluate_split_criteria(plan, *, plan_path) to add repo_root: Path (no existing call sites — CLI is a later step), hashed once, passed into each compute_narrow.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **In plan_tool/split_criteria.py the evaluator borrows code_fingerprint instead of computing it: get the newest saved report via review_persistence.list_saved_reviews(plan_slug, repo_root, plan_path=plan_path) (newest-first) → load_review on the first entry → pass its code_fingerprint ONLY if code_fingerprint_present is True, else omit the key. plan_fingerprint is compute_plan_fingerprint(plan_path); plan_slug is locator.slug_from_filename(plan_path). code_fingerprint is recorded context for later cross-plan analysis, NOT part of the drift decision (which keys on plan_fingerprint + fires? results).** — split_criteria.py is a leaf and cannot import scope_guard/drift_detection to walk the repo, so a fresh code fingerprint is impossible here; the saved-report sidecar already carries one. An author who tries to compute it breaks the leaf posture, and one who keys on 'a report exists' rather than code_fingerprint_present records a value that was never computed. _(when: when a plan-tool step records or borrows a code/plan fingerprint from split_criteria.py or another cycle-free leaf)_ _(e.g. Step 5's evaluate_split_criteria records plan_fingerprint always and code_fingerprint conditionally (present-flag gate), using only the already-imported telemetry/review_persistence seams plus locator.slug_from_filename.)_
- `[cross-step]` **The per-plan split-criteria evaluator is the telemetry RECORDER site (evaluate_split_criteria calls record_plan_criteria_breakdown at the end), so step 6's cmd_split_criteria CLI handler must NOT record — unlike cmd_convergence, which records at the CLI layer because its evaluator doesn't. This is the same double-count trap the convergence template hides: cloning cmd_convergence verbatim would record twice.** — record_plan_criteria_breakdown lives inside the evaluator (so any caller gets telemetry), whereas convergence records at the CLI; an author cloning the convergence command as the template for the new read-only diagnostic must delete the record_* call, matching the captured 'thin CLI wrapper over a function that already emits telemetry must not repeat it' rule. _(when: when a plan-tool step wires the split-criteria CLI or reasons about where the plan-criteria-breakdown telemetry event is emitted)_ _(e.g. Step 5 records inside evaluate_split_criteria; the Deferred and acceptance both state cmd_split_criteria (step 6) records nothing.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **To actuate the scope-out carve from a diagnosis, reuse convergence_diagnosis.classify_fork(diagnosis).step_focus as the carve target — on the FORK_SCOPE_OUT arm it always carries the concrete step number, the SAME one _scope_out_command already prints. Do not re-parse the diagnosis or re-derive --step N; pass rec.step_focus straight into scope_out_step(carved_id=…) so the flag applies exactly the carve the operator saw printed. Actuate only when rec.fork == FORK_SCOPE_OUT and rec.step_focus is not None; FORK_LOCALIZED (→ plan-tool split) and FORK_STRUCTURAL (→ re-seed) are different remedies the scope-out flag must never fire.** — The render already computed the carve step; re-deriving it risks disagreeing with what convergence printed, and firing on FORK_LOCALIZED/FORK_STRUCTURAL would run the wrong structural remedy. classify_fork is pure over the diagnosis, so the actuation reads the same value the render did. _(when: when a plan-tool step actuates or reasons about the scope-out carve target off a convergence diagnosis)_ _(e.g. Step 1: rec = classify_fork(diagnosis); actuate scope_out_step(carved_id=rec.step_focus, allow_scope_out=True, yes=args.yes) only on FORK_SCOPE_OUT, and print a 'no scope-out carve recommended' info line for every other verdict/fork.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **scope_out.scope_out_step owns the ENTIRE apply-or-recommend gate and returns a frozen ScopeOutResult whose outcome ∈ applied / recommended / unsafe / empty-plan / step-missing (only 'applied' mutates); a caller passes allow_scope_out=True + yes=<bool> and then branches on result.outcome to render one line per outcome and returns 0 for ALL of them — a refusal/recommendation is not a failure-to-complete. It records no telemetry and writes no run-log entry (the mutation is journaled inside apply_narrow), so a caller must add neither.** — The five-outcome contract and the 'every outcome exits 0' convention are load-bearing for staying consistent with cmd_scope_out and with convergence's always-exits-0 posture; adding a telemetry recorder or run-log entry here would be an out-of-family, double-logged event. _(when: when a plan-tool step calls scope_out_step from a new caller and must render its result / decide on telemetry)_ _(e.g. Step 1 branches on ScopeOutResult.outcome mirroring cmd_scope_out's messages (seed path + renumber on applied, blocker list on unsafe), returns 0 for every outcome, and adds no record_* call because record_convergence already logged the diagnosis.)_
- `[detail-authoring]` **To make a convergence test resolve FORK_SCOPE_OUT you must craft a HIGH-severity, non-improving recurring region (last_severity ≥ high AND a non-decreasing first→last trend) — the existing tests/cli/test_convergence_cmd.py helper _correctness_rec is severity='medium', which forks to FORK_LOCALIZED, not scope-out. A scope-out-path test needs a new high-severity recurring-region helper plus a real multi-step plan with a carvable edge step.** — classify_fork's scope-out arm is gated on severity+trend, so reusing the medium-severity helper silently exercises the localized-split arm instead; an author cloning existing convergence tests will test the wrong fork. _(when: when a plan-tool step writes tests that must drive convergence into the FORK_SCOPE_OUT arm)_ _(e.g. Step 1's Tests section adds a high-severity non-improving recurring-region helper (the existing _correctness_rec is medium → FORK_LOCALIZED) to drive test_apply_scope_out_carves_on_scope_out_fork.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/detail.py:merge_steps(plan_path, merge_ids=…, repo_root=…, dry_run=True, author_details=False) runs every validity guard (≥2 distinct ids / unknown id / non-canonical numbering / mixed-scope → DetailError) in order and returns a preview MergeResult with NO disk write and NO Claude — use it inside try/except DetailError as a bridge's validity gate rather than re-deriving the checks.** — The bridge must refuse exactly what merge_steps refuses; the executor already owns the guard order, so dry_run reuses it verbatim without mutation or spend. _(when: when a plan-tool step validates a merge set the way merge_steps does, or wraps merge_steps behind a gate)_ _(e.g. Step 2's merge bridge maps a caught DetailError from the dry_run call to its `invalid` refusal outcome.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/detail.py:_merge_is_safe(plan, merge_ids) → (safe, blocking_ids) computes max(merge_ids) and does NOT check membership or non-emptiness, so it MUST run AFTER a validity gate that proves the ids exist; it is the run-state gate merge_steps consults (a non-PENDING member OR a non-PENDING step after the region blocks).** — Calling _merge_is_safe on a malformed/empty set raises or mis-answers via the unguarded max(); the settled order is validity gate first, then _merge_is_safe, then opt-in/confirm. _(when: when a plan-tool step calls or orders _merge_is_safe relative to a validity check)_ _(e.g. Step 2's bridge order: re-parse → dry_run validity → _merge_is_safe → allow_merge → _confirm_merge → merge_steps apply.)_
- `[cross-step]` **plan-tool's apply-or-recommend bridges split on whether they mint a review.Recommendation: escalate_to_split builds _structural_split_rec because its create-loop caller needs a surfaced rec; the merge bridge and scope_out_step mint NONE because their callers already hold the triggering finding (granularity-merge / the diagnosis). So a 'no new Recommendation source token' constraint is honored cleanly by minting no rec at all — returning outcome + the acted-on set (+ blocking on unsafe).** — An author copying escalate_to_split reflexively adds a rec; but that only exists because escalate's caller lacks the finding, whereas merge/scope-out callers already carry it — adding a rec would both over-scope and mint a source token the constraint forbids. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds an apply-or-recommend bridge and must decide whether it mints a review.Recommendation)_ _(e.g. Step 2's merge bridge returns a frozen result carrying the merge set and MergeResult, and builds no Recommendation, because step 5's walk already holds the granularity-merge finding that fired it.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **The merge primitives (MergeResult, merge_steps, _merge_is_safe, _confirm_merge) all live in plan_tool/detail.py — there is no merge.py — so a merge-adjacent primitive belongs beside them (after merge_steps, so it can call it); its tests go in tests/test_detail.py reusing the existing _build_merge_plan helper (canonical 4-step plan, accepts statuses={id: StepStatus}) and the _GOOD_BODY seven-section constant.** — scope_out and split_criteria are their own modules, so an author expects merge in a merge.py and mis-locates the bridge; knowing the primitives + test fixtures already live in detail.py/test_detail.py avoids a wrong-file edit and a re-authored fixture. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds or tests a merge-related primitive)_ _(e.g. Step 2 placed MergeBridgeResult + merge_bridge in detail.py after merge_steps and added TestMergeBridge to test_detail.py reusing _build_merge_plan / _GOOD_BODY.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/schema.py:Step._scope_status_coherent RAISES if a parked step (scope deferred/wont_do) is set to current/done — so any actuator that sets StepStatus.DONE or CURRENT must refuse non-COMMITTED named steps up front (outcome="unsafe"), or the illegal state reaches write_plan's re-validation and crashes. Committed-scope is the precondition for a mark-done/promote actuator.** — write_plan re-validates the Plan, so an actuator that flips a parked step done produces a state the model rejects at serialization time; the coherence check is the load-bearing invariant that forces the up-front scope gate rather than letting the write blow up. _(when: when a plan-tool step sets StepStatus.DONE/CURRENT on operator- or finding-named steps)_ _(e.g. Step 3's reground_bridge safety gate: any named id whose scope != StepScope.COMMITTED → outcome="unsafe" with the parked id in blocking, refused before mark_steps_done runs.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **The "mark step(s) done → promote next_runnable_step to CURRENT → flip PlanStatus.COMPLETED when all_steps_done" cursor wrapper now lives in THREE places — launcher.py:mark_done_and_advance, scope_out.py:compute_narrow's cursor/status blocks, and reground.py:mark_steps_done — all leaning on Plan.current_step / next_runnable_step / all_steps_done, so the underlying rule is single-sourced on the model and only the thin set-status-and-flip wrapper repeats. A new leaf actuator RE-DERIVES the wrapper over the Plan methods; it must NOT import launcher.mark_done_and_advance (that drags a heavy orchestrator into the leaf). Consolidating the wrapper is a reconcile/refactor item, not a feature step.** — An author reaching for the existing mark_done_and_advance to avoid re-typing the cursor logic breaks the leaf posture; the rule that actually matters (which step is next-runnable) already lives on the Plan model, so re-deriving the thin wrapper duplicates nothing load-bearing and keeps the import graph acyclic. _(when: when a plan-tool leaf needs the mark-done/promote-cursor/flip-completed logic and is tempted to import launcher.mark_done_and_advance)_ _(e.g. Step 3's reground.py imports only parser/schema/locator + stdlib and re-derives the cursor block over Plan methods, with 'consolidate the shared wrapper' explicitly Deferred as a refactor detail can't mint.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan-tool's re-ground remedy is its OWN module plan_tool/reground.py (a cycle-free leaf), NOT part of detail.py where the merge primitives live — the re-ground bridge is deliberately not merge and must import no merge symbol (detail.merge_steps / merge_bridge). This keeps _reground_already_built_recommendation's granularity-merge literal on the neutral triage_reason path and off the split/merge actuators, even though it reuses that literal. reground.py is the fourth apply-or-recommend gate (after launcher.escalate_to_split, scope_out.scope_out_step, detail.merge_bridge), modeled closest on scope_out_step (zero Claude, no invoker= seam).** — The granularity-merge finding's remedy is re-ground/re-baseline, not structural merge; routing the bridge through detail.merge_steps would conflate the two and defeat the neutral-triage guard that keeps the re-ground finding off the split path. Placing the bridge in its own leaf (not detail.py) enforces that separation structurally. _(when: when a plan-tool step actuates the reconcile-lane granularity-merge (re-ground) finding, or reasons about where the re-ground bridge lives vs the merge primitives)_ _(e.g. Step 3 placed RegroundResult + mark_steps_done + reground_bridge in a new plan_tool/reground.py importing only parser/schema/locator, with acceptance pinning that it imports neither plan_tool.launcher nor plan_tool.detail and calls no merge primitive.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **`granularity-merge` is a TWO-producer source with DIFFERENT record shapes that a router must discriminate: `granularity.py:_merge_rec` sets `step_id=lo` and hides both contiguous members in the fingerprint, while `review.py:_reground_already_built_recommendation` sets `step_id=None` and hides a variable-length already-built id set in its fingerprint. The split-side `split_predicate_key` recovery does NOT generalize to it (variable-length set). The shared directive grammar (`MergeAction`, `render_merge_action`, `parse_merge_action`, `MERGE_ACTION_MERGE`/`_REGROUND`) must live in `review.py`, not `granularity.py`, because `granularity` imports `review` and `review` must never import `granularity` — the same cycle reason `_GRANULARITY_MERGE_SOURCE` is a duplicated literal.** — A step 5-style walk routing merge findings to `merge_bridge` and re-ground findings to `reground_bridge` (two remedies the plan says must never be conflated) needs the exact shape difference and a recovery path both producers can reach without the forbidden reverse import; guessing either mis-routes the finding or introduces a cycle. _(when: when a plan-tool step reads, classifies, or routes a granularity-merge finding, or exposes a machine key off one)_ _(e.g. Step 4 placed the two kind constants + `MergeAction` + builder/parser near `_GRANULARITY_MERGE_SOURCE` in `review.py`; `_reground_already_built_recommendation` calls the builder directly and `granularity.py:_merge_rec` imports it, keeping the one-way `granularity → review` edge.)_
- `[detail-authoring]` **Adding a parseable directive to a granularity/review finding's `suggested_action` is id-safe: `_make_rec_id` hashes `(step_id, source, fingerprint)` and `suggested_action` is not in it, so appending a marker leaves every existing rec id byte-stable — pin this with the existing `test_ids_are_stable` (granularity) and `test_reground_id_stable_for_same_set` (review) staying green, plus a 'building twice yields same id' test. Do NOT fold the directive into the fingerprint.** — An author worried the appended marker changes recovery could reflexively add it to the fingerprint to 'make it recoverable', which would move every id and break the stability tests; the correct move is marker-in-suggested_action, fingerprint untouched. _(when: when a plan-tool step mutates a granularity/review Recommendation's suggested_action and must preserve rec id stability)_ _(e.g. Step 4's `test_merge_directive_does_not_change_rec_id` / `test_reground_directive_does_not_change_rec_id` guard that the marker sits outside the hashed fingerprint.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/review_walk.py routes a finding to an actuator only when ONE of its dispatch-path predicates is truthy — recognized_action (plan-tool detail --step shape) / should_apply_as_finding (_APPLY_AS_FINDING_SOURCES) / file_check_create_target / now merge_remedy_target — and is_dispatchable ORs them. Adding a new bridge means adding a predicate near file_check_create_target AND a fourth clause in is_dispatchable; auto-dispatch (walk_recommendations / _prompt_for_annotation / _auto_apply) all gate on is_dispatchable. Import the predicate's parser from plan_tool.review (review_walk already imports review; review never imports review_walk — no cycle), never from granularity.** — Without both the predicate and the is_dispatchable clause the walk falls to the terminal 'run it manually in another shell' notice and never invokes action_fn for the finding; importing the parser from granularity would risk the forbidden reverse edge. _(when: when a plan-tool step wires a finding source to actuate a bridge through the review/reconcile walk, or reasons about how the walk decides a finding is dispatchable)_ _(e.g. Step 5 added merge_remedy_target(rec)=parse_merge_action(rec.suggested_action) beside file_check_create_target and a `if merge_remedy_target(rec) is not None: return True` clause in is_dispatchable, importing parse_merge_action from plan_tool.review.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **In plan_tool/cli/review_actions.py the per-source dispatchers are closures inside _build_review_action_fn (_dispatch_structural_escalation, _dispatch_file_check_create, now _dispatch_merge_remedy), each using BODY-LOCAL imports of its actuator so tests patch the actuator on its OWNING module (plan_tool.detail.merge_bridge, plan_tool.reground.reground_bridge) not a cli global, and each controls annotation status via state.apply_skip: leave it False (default) on the mutated/`applied` outcome so the walk records `applied`, set it True on EVERY other outcome (recommended/unsafe/invalid/noop/step-missing) so the walk records `skip`. Route the new branch in action(rec) after the file_check_create_target check and before the `if not rec.suggested_action` terminal.** — The apply_skip flag is the sole lever that tells the walk whether a finding was resolved; getting it wrong marks an un-mutated recommend/refuse as resolved (or vice versa). Body-local imports keep review_actions import-light and let tests patch on the owning module the dispatcher resolves at call time. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a dispatcher branch to cli/review_actions.py:_build_review_action_fn or reasons about how a bridge outcome maps to the walk's recorded annotation)_ _(e.g. Step 5's _dispatch_merge_remedy sets state.apply_skip=True for recommended/unsafe/invalid/noop/step-missing and leaves it False only on `applied`, mirroring _dispatch_file_check_create.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **When dispatching a granularity-merge finding to a bridge from the walk, forward the target step ids from the PARSED directive (step 4's parse_merge_action / MergeAction) verbatim into the bridge's merge-set / step-ids argument — NEVER from rec.step_id, which is the low member id for a _merge_rec finding and None for a re-ground finding. The full id set is readable only from the suggested_action directive (that directive exists precisely because the set is unrecoverable from the hashed rec id). Branch merge-vs-reground on the parsed directive KIND (MERGE_ACTION_MERGE / MERGE_ACTION_REGROUND), never on the shared granularity-merge source string.** — rec.step_id under-specifies the target set (low-id-only or None), and the granularity-merge source is shared by both producers so it can't discriminate merge from re-ground — keying on it would conflate a structural merge with a re-ground, the exact confusion the plan forbids. _(when: when a plan-tool step routes a granularity-merge finding to merge_bridge vs reground_bridge, or extracts the target step set from such a finding)_ _(e.g. Step 5's _dispatch_merge_remedy reads parse_merge_action once, routes MERGE_ACTION_MERGE→merge_bridge / MERGE_ACTION_REGROUND→reground_bridge, and passes directive.step ids into each bridge.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan-tool's structural-remedy model is documented in PARALLEL across CLAUDE.md and RUNBOOK.md, so a change to any structural-remedy behavior must edit both: CLAUDE.md carries it in the **Granularity advisor**, **Convergence diagnostic**, and **Structural remedy vocabulary** Architecture paragraphs; RUNBOOK.md carries it in the **completeness** granularity-merge paragraph, the **per-subcommand reconcile** re-ground callout, the **Diagnosing convergence** remedy fork + 'four structural remedies as one model' block, the **Carve a spinning region** section, and the review **walk-through** apply-paths list.** — The recommend-only / hand-run-merge / four-remedies wording is restated in both docs' parallel sections; editing one and not the other leaves the two docs disagreeing about whether a remedy is actuatable, and the sections are easy to miss because they're spread across each file. _(when: when a plan-tool step changes structural-remedy behavior (split/merge/scope-out/re-ground bridges or their gates) and must update the docs)_ _(e.g. Step 6 had to touch three CLAUDE.md paragraphs and five RUNBOOK sections to describe the same three bridges (merge_bridge / reground_bridge / --apply-scope-out) and drop the stale recommend-only wording in every one.)_

Do not scope a drift-guard test into a CLAUDE.md/RUNBOOK edit, and do not expect one to catch a stale claim.** — An author reflexively looks for the drift-guard test that would catch a stale doc claim; none exists for these two files, so the verification must be explicit greps rather than a byte-match assertion, and the step is genuinely test-free. _(when: when a plan-tool step edits CLAUDE.md or RUNBOOK.md and reasons about whether a drift-guard test applies)_ _(e.g. Step 6's Verification notes CLAUDE.md/RUNBOOK are not generated under docs/cli/, so no cli_reference-style test covers them — the gate is the stale-phrase and symbol-existence greps, with 'suite stays green' as the only automated check.)_
