- `[detail-authoring]` **tests/test_jira.py:TestRenderJiraPrompt is the regression surface for Jira prompt wrapper contracts, including missing files, unreadable files, creates/(new), no-files, fenced blocks, truncation markers, and append/covered-step annotations.** — The prompt excerpt change is allowed to alter readable source selection, not the surrounding Jira prompt shape or marker vocabulary. _(when: when detail changes plan_tool/jira.py prompt rendering or file-content blocks)_ _(e.g. Add the symbol-past-byte-cap test under TestRenderJiraPrompt and keep existing marker/append tests green.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/annotate.py separates implementation grounding from step-spec loading: _ground_source owns the ## Code grounding file bodies, while _load_step_specs still uses _bound_for_block for detail/spec text.** — Specs are the artifact being judged against, not implementation evidence; applying source excerpt behavior to both would blur annotate's prompt contract and confidence rules. _(when: when editing annotate prompt grounding, PlanAnnotation evidence, or max_file_bytes behavior)_ _(e.g. Step 6 should replace only _ground_source's successful-read _bound_for_block(body, max_file_bytes) path, leaving _load_step_specs bounded by _bound_for_block.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **Annotate grounding owns path extraction and accounting in plan_tool/annotate.py: extract_file_path_candidates, umbrella-root resolution, detail-file exclusion, duplicate/missing/binary/unreadable skips, grounded_files, and grounding_* counts must stay there; prompt_excerpt.py only selects text after a readable file is obtained.** — Low-grounding demotion and skip reporting depend on annotate's existing candidate/count semantics, so moving filesystem or skip logic into the excerpt helper would change PlanAnnotation behavior. _(when: when changing plan_tool/annotate.py:_ground_source or adding source excerpting to annotate)_ _(e.g. _ground_source should call the excerpt helper only after _read_grounding_text returns text, preserving skip_reasons and resolved Path tuples unchanged.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **Annotate has no reliable per-file step owner, so candidate symbols should be broad but bounded: parse plan input with _try_parse_plan when possible, reuse review._derive_symbols for step titles/headings/prose tokens, and avoid adding a second tokenizer in annotate.py.** — The project already centralizes title-to-symbol filtering in review._derive_symbols, and annotate can receive rough notes as well as plans, so a conservative shared candidate list is the settled shape. _(when: when annotate.py needs symbol candidates for grounding excerpts)_ _(e.g. For non-plan notes, derive candidates from markdown headings or compact nearby prose; for plans, gather from step titles, then de-duplicate and cap before calling prompt_excerpt.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **Annotate's grounded block wrapper is load-bearing: keep headers as ### `path`, keep fenced code blocks, keep GroundedSource.files as (Path, str), and keep PlanAnnotation.grounded_files/counts based on resolved files rather than excerpt success.** — Tests and downstream confidence logic key off the block shape and grounding counts; symbol-aware snippets may change selected text but not the surrounding annotation contract. _(when: when editing render_annotate_prompt inputs, _format_grounded_block, or annotate grounding tests)_ _(e.g. tests/test_annotate.py should capture the prompt for symbol-past-cap behavior while keeping existing low-grounding and detail-file-exclusion tests green.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **In plan-tool prompt cleanup, _MAX_DETAIL_PARSE_BYTES in review.py is not a prompt excerpt budget and must remain separate from prompt_excerpt's shared source-preview default.** — It bounds deterministic detail-body parsing, not readable implementation file previews, so collapsing it into the shared excerpt cap would couple unrelated behavior. _(when: when editing plan_tool/review.py prompt excerpt constants or byte caps)_ _(e.g. Step 7 may remove local source-preview caps from review prompt paths, but _MAX_DETAIL_PARSE_BYTES stays.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **In annotate.py, _bound_for_block may remain after source excerpt cleanup if _load_step_specs still uses it for detail/spec text; only _ground_source's readable code grounding should move to prompt_excerpt.** — Implementation grounding and step-spec loading are separate prompt surfaces with different evidence roles. _(when: when editing plan_tool/annotate.py truncation or prompt grounding helpers)_ _(e.g. Step 7 removes old code-grounding head slicing from _ground_source but does not force _load_step_specs onto the source excerpt helper.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **After the symbol-aware rollout, plan_tool/prompt_excerpt.py should be the only owner of readable implementation/source excerpt selection and the default source-preview budget; detail.py, review.py, jira.py, and annotate.py should only own filesystem handling and wrapper text.** — Leaving local readable-file slicing or duplicated source-preview caps in those prompt callers creates two sources of truth and can silently revive head-slicing in one surface. _(when: when changing readable source file previews in plan_tool/detail.py, review.py, jira.py, or annotate.py)_ _(e.g. Step 7's scoped callers are _format_files_contents_block, render_review_prompt, _collect_done_step_file_contents, _format_audit_detail_bundle, _render_step_files_contents, and _ground_source.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **RUNBOOK.md's prompt excerpt policy belongs in `Inspecting prompts before they run`, with reconcile asymmetry notes in the `detail --reconcile` and `reconcile-code` sections.** — Those are the operator locations that already teach dry-run prompt inspection and plan-vs-code repair direction; scattering the policy elsewhere would be less discoverable. _(when: when editing plan-tool docs for prompt excerpt behavior or run/detail reconcile context differences)_ _(e.g. Step 8 scopes the policy to `RUNBOOK.md:Inspecting prompts before they run`, `detail --reconcile — fix the plan to match the code`, and `reconcile-code — fix the code to match the plan`.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **For plan-tool prompt excerpt docs, `_(truncated)_` remains the stable operator-facing marker; docs should say it means a bounded preview, not a missing rest-of-file or complete file view.** — The symbol-aware rollout changes where readable source previews start, but existing prompt wrappers and marker vocabulary remain load-bearing. _(when: when documenting or reviewing plan-tool prompt source-preview behavior)_ _(e.g. Step 8 acceptance pins that focused excerpts do not imply the rest of the file is absent and that `_(truncated)_` still marks an incomplete preview.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/style.py is the single owner of color-gated diagnostic output (`warn` = yellow 'warning:' prefix to stderr; `color_enabled` honors NO_COLOR / PLAN_TOOL_FORCE_COLOR / TTY) and is itself a cycle-free leaf (only imports plan_tool.schema under TYPE_CHECKING). A new leaf that must emit a TTY-aware/plain-on-pipe advisory reuses style.warn/color_enabled rather than a raw print — that is the one acceptable first-party import for an otherwise stdlib-only leaf and it introduces no cycle.** — Routing a new advisory through style.warn makes it look like every other tool diagnostic and gets NO_COLOR/force-color/TTY gating for free, while keeping the leaf's import graph acyclic — the exact posture telemetry.py enforces (which imports nothing first-party). _(when: when a plan-tool leaf/diagnostic needs color-gated or TTY-aware stderr output and would otherwise reach for print())_ _(e.g. prompt_budget.py (stdlib-only otherwise) imports only plan_tool.style for maybe_warn_prompt_budget's advisory; test_leaf_imports_are_cycle_free pins that stdlib + plan_tool.style are the sole imports.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **In plan_tool, prompt byte size is already computed in several places as ACCOUNTING ONLY — backend.py:prompt_bytes, launcher.py:_streaming_prompt_bytes, logged through shell.py and run_log.py — but nothing compares it to a budget before sending; overflow is only recognized AFTER the fact via claude_errors.ClaudeFailureKind.CONTEXT_OVERFLOW. A pre-flight budget/limit leaf consumes those existing byte totals rather than recomputing, and does not touch those accounting call sites.** — A future plan touching prompt sizing needs to know the measuring already exists (don't re-derive prompt_bytes) and that the gap is comparison-against-a-budget, not measurement — so the new work is a leaf the wiring steps feed, not an edit to the accounting paths. _(when: when a plan-tool step measures prompt size or adds a pre-flight token/context-budget check)_ _(e.g. The prompt-budget-advisory plan lands prompt_budget.py as the shared measuring stick; steps 3–7 feed backend/launcher byte totals into it and leave prompt_bytes/_streaming_prompt_bytes unchanged.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/model_specs.py:ModelSpec.context_window holds the per-model context window (Anthropic entries are ~200K class), but a cycle-free leaf must NOT import model_specs to fetch it — the caller resolves the window and passes context_window in, and the leaf falls back to a named DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW (200_000) when None.** — Importing model_specs into a would-be leaf drags catalog-resolution logic across the leaf boundary; keeping the window an injected parameter preserves the leaf posture and lets the per-backend window source evolve without touching the leaf. _(when: when a plan-tool leaf needs a model's context-window value and is tempted to import model_specs)_ _(e.g. prompt_budget.py defines DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW=200_000 (matching ModelSpec.context_window's Anthropic class) but imports no model_specs; context_window is a kwarg callers supply.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **Adding a new decision family to plan_tool/telemetry.py has a fixed, small footprint: a `record_X` passthrough placed in the `# --- per-kind convenience recorders ---` block (after the last sibling, before read_decisions) that builds a context dict and delegates to record_decision (inheriting the best-effort write, byte cap, and swallow-all-errors guard for free), two module literal constants (`X_KIND` / `X_DECISION`) mirroring PLAN_CRITERIA_BREAKDOWN_KIND/PLAN_CRITERIA_DECISION, a `#### <Name>` subsection under DATA_CONTRACT.md's Decision-telemetry section plus the new literal added to the DecisionEvent `kind` row, and per-kind tests in tests/test_telemetry.py + a context-keys drift test in tests/test_data_contract.py. It is NOT a DecisionEvent field change and does NOT bump TELEMETRY_SCHEMA_VERSION.** — An author cloning a recorder either over-scopes (bumps the schema version, edits the field-existence guard) or under-scopes (forgets the kind-row edit or the context-keys drift test, so the new keys go undocumented). The set is stable across the existing five recorders; treating it as the canonical new-kind footprint avoids both. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a new decision kind/recorder to plan_tool/telemetry.py)_ _(e.g. Step 2's record_prompt_budget mirrors record_convergence/record_plan_criteria_breakdown: it takes only ints/strings/list (keeping telemetry.py stdlib-only), omits each optional key when None (missing key = not-applicable, per record_create_step_outcome), and delegates to record_decision(kind=PROMPT_BUDGET_KIND, decision=PROMPT_BUDGET_DECISION, ...).)_
- `[cross-step]` **A telemetry recorder must stay a primitives-only seam: it takes plain ints/strings/lists and never imports the domain type it records (e.g. prompt_budget.PromptBudget / its LEVEL_* constants) — the caller in each wiring step projects the domain object to primitives (budget.level, budget.total_bytes, list-of-pairs for a tuple field) before calling. This keeps telemetry.py's 'imports nothing first-party' leaf posture intact and lets the recorder step land independently of the step that defines the domain type.** — Importing the recorded domain type into telemetry.py breaks its stdlib-only leaf invariant and couples the recorder step to the domain-type step's ordering. Because every existing recorder already projects at the call site, following that discipline lets the recorder ship before its callers exist and keeps the import graph acyclic. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a telemetry recorder for a value produced by a domain type defined in a sibling/earlier step)_ _(e.g. Step 2's record_prompt_budget takes advisory as a plain str (caller passes budget.level) and stores blocks (a tuple[tuple[str,int],...]) as [[name, bytes], ...] since JSON has no tuples; the PromptBudget→primitives projection is deferred to wiring steps 3–7, so step 2 lands with no import of plan_tool.prompt_budget.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/detail.py:_author_step_detail is the SINGLE real-invoke seam in the detail authoring path: it is called by both generate_detail's serial loop (outcome = _author_step_detail(...)) and _generate_detail_concurrent's _run_worker, and it returns early in the `if resumed:` branch (checkpoint resume) BEFORE the real-invoke else-branch that runs the attempt loop. Any per-authored-step hook (advisory, telemetry, instrumentation) belongs in that else-branch, before the `for attempt in range(...)` loop — placing it there fires once per step, covers both paths in one edit, and never fires for a resumed step.** — An author who instruments generate_detail's loop misses the concurrent path (and vice versa), and an author who instruments before the resumed check warns on prompts that are never sent; the seam is the one place both conditions are already correct. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a per-authored-step hook to the detail authoring path)_ _(e.g. Step 3 put maybe_warn_prompt_budget + record_prompt_budget in _author_step_detail's invoke else-branch, before the retry loop, using total_bytes = len(prompt.encode('utf-8')) matching the run log's claude_call_start byte count.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **detail.py:_author_step_detail receives prompt/step/repo_root/plan_slug but NOT plan / sibling_details / prior_body, so it cannot rebuild per-block prompt sizes itself. A hook needing block-level data must accept it as a new keyword arg (default empty, e.g. budget_blocks: Sequence[tuple[str,int]] = ()) that EACH render site fills — the serial render_detail_prompt(...) call in generate_detail and the concurrent one in _generate_detail_concurrent — computed by a single module helper that calls the SAME formatters render_detail_prompt substitutes.** — The seam has repo_root and plan_slug in hand (so telemetry is easy) but is downstream of prompt assembly, so block decomposition must be threaded in from the two render sites; recomputing it inside the seam is impossible and re-deriving it differently would drift from the actual prompt. _(when: when a plan-tool step needs per-block prompt content inside _author_step_detail or wires a helper that must track render_detail_prompt's substitutions)_ _(e.g. The named detail blocks come from _format_files_contents_block, _format_sibling_details_block, _format_prior_body_block, the plan-references block, render_lessons_block(load_lessons(...)), and _format_already_implemented_block — a _detail_budget_blocks helper calls those exact formatters and is invoked at both render sites, passing its result into _author_step_detail.)_
- `[detail-authoring]` **In detail.py, leaf functions consumed by the authoring path must be imported at MODULE TOP (not lazily) so tests can monkeypatch plan_tool.detail.<name> — this mirrors why plan_tool.launcher and apply_finding are imported module-level (the existing comment on the launcher import already states 'module-level so tests can monkeypatch'). plan_tool.telemetry (stdlib-only leaf) and plan_tool.prompt_budget (near-leaf importing only stdlib + plan_tool.style) both import into detail.py without a cycle.** — A body-local import of the leaf would make the spy target unreachable for the test convention this file uses (spy by monkeypatching the module-level name), and an author unsure about cycles might reach for a lazy import unnecessarily — both prompt_budget and telemetry are cycle-safe at detail.py's top. _(when: when a plan-tool step imports prompt_budget/telemetry (or another leaf) into detail.py and tests must spy on it)_ _(e.g. Step 3 added module-top imports of estimate_prompt_budget, maybe_warn_prompt_budget, and record_prompt_budget beside the existing plan_tool.launcher import; tests spy via monkeypatching plan_tool.detail.maybe_warn_prompt_budget / estimate_prompt_budget / record_prompt_budget.)_
- `[detail-authoring]` **detail --dry-run's prompt text is printed to STDOUT by cli/detail's cmd_detail (so a piped `detail --dry-run` yields a clean prompt), so any dry-run diagnostic added inside generate_detail's `if dry_run:` branch must go to STDERR to avoid corrupting that stdout artifact, and must skip record_prompt_budget entirely (dry-run sends nothing).** — Operators pipe dry-run to capture the prompt; mixing a breakdown into stdout breaks that, and recording telemetry for an un-sent prompt pollutes the pre-send distribution. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds output to generate_detail's dry_run branch)_ _(e.g. Step 3's dry-run branch builds budget_blocks, calls estimate_prompt_budget directly, prints the breakdown to stderr per step, and does not call record_prompt_budget; test_dry_run_prints_breakdown_and_does_not_invoke captures stderr with capsys.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/create.py has THREE separate real-invoke send functions — propose_distilled_seed_from_claude (distill), propose_steps_from_claude (step proposal, called twice in create_plan), and propose_body_sections (synthesis) — NOT one funnel like detail.py's _author_step_detail. Each has the identical shape: a `if cached is not None:` resume branch (reuses checkpointed raw, no send) paired with an `else:` branch that computes `prompt_bytes = len(prompt.encode('utf-8'))` then calls `raw = invoker(prompt)`, and each has a one-shot repair-retry reprompt. A per-send hook is a shared helper called from all three else-branches, reusing the existing prompt_bytes rather than recomputing.** — An author who assumes create mirrors detail's single-seam shape will either miss two of the three phases or recompute a byte total the phase already holds; the three-function fan-out plus the twice-called steps function is the load-bearing structural fact for any create-path pre-send instrumentation. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds pre-send instrumentation (advisory/telemetry/budget) to create.py or reasons about where create's Claude phases send)_ _(e.g. Step 4's prompt-budget wiring: three prompt_bytes sites at create.py:1428 (steps), 2706 (synthesis), 3070 (distill), each in an else-branch; the phase content blocks (seed / description+lessons_block / seed+reference_docs) are already in local scope. A fourth prompt_bytes at 2202 belongs to a Deferred create phase.)_
- `[detail-authoring]` **In tests/test_create.py, exercise the propose_* send functions by importing them directly from plan_tool.create and driving each with a fake invoker + NullReporter (per TestProposeStepsFromClaudeProgress / TestProposeBodySectionsFromClaude); spy on wired leaf/recorder seams by monkeypatching the module-level names on plan_tool.create (e.g. plan_tool.create.maybe_warn_prompt_budget). The distill function's round-trip tests live in tests/test_distill.py, but create-phase wiring tests belong in tests/test_create.py since all three propose_* functions are importable from plan_tool.create.** — The propose_* functions are unit-testable in isolation without driving create_plan end-to-end, and the spy-by-module-level-monkeypatch convention only works if the wired leaf names are imported at create.py's top — so a wiring step's tests go in test_create.py against the functions, not integration tests through the wizard. _(when: when a plan-tool step tests behavior wired into one of create.py's propose_* send functions)_ _(e.g. Step 4's advisory tests drive propose_distilled_seed_from_claude / propose_steps_from_claude / propose_body_sections directly and monkeypatch plan_tool.create.{maybe_warn_prompt_budget,estimate_prompt_budget,record_prompt_budget}, even though distill's own round-trip tests live in test_distill.py.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **The conceptual plan-audit path in plan_tool/review.py is a two-tier loop: audit_plan_until_stable is the once-per-run driver (its `while passes < cap:` loop), and check_plan_audit is the per-pass function holding the real send + `for attempt in (1, 2):` retry. Pre-send instrumentation (advisory/telemetry/budget) goes ONCE before audit_plan_until_stable's loop — NOT in check_plan_audit — because each pass re-audits the same plan (only the bounded carried-findings block grows). The base audit prompt is render_plan_audit_prompt(plan, plan_path, repo_root=..., empty carried_findings), which returns None when the plan has no body (None prompt = no send = no advisory), so gate the hook on `invoker is not None` AND that base prompt not None.** — An author who assumes the audit path funnels through one send-seam (like detail.py's _author_step_detail) will instrument check_plan_audit and nag once per pass; the once-per-run seam is the driver above the loop. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds pre-send instrumentation to the conceptual plan-audit path or reasons about where audit_plan_until_stable vs check_plan_audit sends)_ _(e.g. Step 5's hook: render the base prompt, gate on invoker+prompt, total_bytes = len(prompt.encode('utf-8')), then maybe_warn_prompt_budget + record_prompt_budget once before the pass loop.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **NAME COLLISION in plan_tool/review.py:audit_plan_until_stable — it already has a `budget_report: Optional[dict]` param that is the audit-pass COVERAGE budget (BACKLOG #60c: budget_limited / passes_used / cap), entirely unrelated to prompt-token budget. Any prompt-budget local added here must be named distinctly (e.g. prompt_budget) and must not touch budget_report.** — Reusing/overwriting budget_report or reasoning about it as the token budget silently corrupts the audit-pass coverage accounting, which is a different concern under the same word 'budget'. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a token/prompt-budget value inside audit_plan_until_stable, where `budget_report` already means the audit-pass coverage budget)_ _(e.g. Step 5 named its local prompt_budget and left budget_report behavior unchanged; acceptance pinned 'budget_report behavior is unchanged'.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **The plan-audit prompt's major blocks in plan_tool/review.py are formatted by: plan body = _collect_plan_body(plan_path); detail bundle = _format_audit_detail_bundle(plan, plan_path, repo_root, max_file_bytes=_AUDIT_DETAIL_FILE_BYTES) with _AUDIT_DETAIL_FILE_BYTES=4096 per detail file; detail-bundle status = _format_detail_bundle_status_block(audit_detail_bundle_status(plan, plan_path, repo_root)); carried-findings block bounded by _CARRIED_BLOCK_MAX_FINDINGS / _CARRIED_BODY_EXCERPT_CHARS. A budget-breakdown helper (single-sourced against render_plan_audit_prompt) calls those exact formatters; the carried-findings block is excluded from the base breakdown (empty at base, bounded otherwise).** — A breakdown helper that re-derives block sizes differently would drift from what render_plan_audit_prompt actually ships; these are the load-bearing formatter names for any audit-prompt sizing work. _(when: when a plan-tool step measures, decomposes, or edits the plan-audit prompt's constituent blocks in review.py)_ _(e.g. Step 5's _plan_audit_budget_blocks returns (name, bytes) pairs for 'plan body' / 'detail bundle' / 'detail-bundle status' via those formatters; the block sum is display-only and need not equal len(rendered prompt).)_
- `[detail-authoring]` **review.py follows the same test-spy convention as detail.py/create.py: import wired leaf/recorder seams at MODULE TOP so tests monkeypatch plan_tool.review.<name> (e.g. plan_tool.review.maybe_warn_prompt_budget / record_prompt_budget); exercise audit_plan_until_stable by driving it directly with a fake invoker that returns a well-formed two-section audit response so passes actually run. plan_tool.prompt_budget (stdlib + plan_tool.style only) and plan_tool.telemetry (nothing first-party) both import into review.py without a cycle.** — A body-local import makes the module-level spy target unreachable for this file's monkeypatch convention; both leaves are cycle-safe at review.py's top, so there's no reason to import lazily. _(when: when a plan-tool step wires a leaf/recorder into review.py and tests must spy on it, or drives audit_plan_until_stable in tests)_ _(e.g. Step 5 added module-top imports beside `from plan_tool.style import tool` and tested the once-per-run / once-per-pass / skip-on-no-invoker cases by spying on plan_tool.review.record_prompt_budget while driving audit_plan_until_stable with a productive fake invoker.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/launcher.py:run_step is the SINGLE real-send seam for the run path — run/check/security/reconcile modes all funnel through the one `exit_code, stdout = invoker(prompt)` call, and the `if dry_run:` branch returns BEFORE it. A per-invoke hook (advisory/telemetry) goes on that real-invoke path after the dry-run early return and before the invoke: it fires once per sent step, is mode-agnostic (do NOT gate on `mode in MUTATING_MODES` — prompt size matters for review modes too), and never fires for a dry run. This mirrors detail.py:_author_step_detail's single-seam shape.** — An author who gates the hook on mutating modes misses check/security/reconcile sends, and one who instruments before the dry-run return warns on a prompt that is never sent; the post-dry-run pre-invoke point is the one place both conditions are already correct for all four modes. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds pre-send instrumentation to the run/launcher path or reasons about where run_step sends)_ _(e.g. Step 6 placed maybe_warn_prompt_budget + record_prompt_budget on run_step's real-invoke path with phase="run-step" shared across all modes; test_review_mode_also_warns pins mode="security" still warns.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **launcher._streaming_prompt_bytes(prompt) is the run path's CANONICAL byte measure — the exact number claude_call_start logs — and it is computed inside `if run_logger is not None:`. A run-path prompt-size advisory reuses _streaming_prompt_bytes (NOT len(prompt.encode('utf-8')) as detail/create/review use), and must compute it on the unconditional path so it fires even when run_logger is None. The prompt is measured AFTER `prompt += _test_order_directive(step.change_type)`, matching what claude_call_start logs.** — The run path deliberately uses a different byte function than the other prompt-budget wiring steps; an author who clones detail/create's len(encode) idiom here produces a total that disagrees with the run log, and one who leaves the total inside the run_logger guard silently drops the advisory when no logger is bound. _(when: when a plan-tool step measures the run/launcher prompt size or reuses _streaming_prompt_bytes for an advisory total)_ _(e.g. Step 6's total_bytes = _streaming_prompt_bytes(prompt); test_total_reuses_streaming_prompt_bytes pins the reuse and test_no_run_logger_still_warns pins the unconditional path.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **The run prompt embeds the step's ENTIRE detail file UNCAPPED — renderer._load_detail fills the step_detail template variable with the full file body, with NO per-file cap (unlike the detail/audit paths' _AUDIT_DETAIL_FILE_BYTES=4096) — so run_step assembles the largest per-step prompt the tool sends. A run-prompt block breakdown is single-sourced by calling the same module-private loaders render_prompt substitutes via _build_variables: renderer._load_detail (dominant block) and renderer._load_lessons_section.** — Any run-prompt sizing/decomposition work must know the detail embed is uncapped (that is why the advisory matters most here) and must reuse _load_detail/_load_lessons_section rather than re-deriving block sizes, or the breakdown drifts from the shipped prompt; overflow today is only caught after the fact via ClaudeFailureKind.CONTEXT_OVERFLOW. _(when: when a plan-tool step measures, decomposes, or edits the run prompt's constituent blocks in launcher.py / renderer.py)_ _(e.g. Step 6's _run_budget_blocks(plan, step, repo_root) returns ("step detail", len(_load_detail(...))) and ("lessons", len(_load_lessons_section(...))); capping the uncapped embed was left to BACKLOG (#95 follow-up).)_
- `[detail-authoring]` **plan_tool/launcher.py does NOT import slug_from_filename from plan_tool.locator today — a run-path step that records telemetry keyed on a plan slug must add that import and derive plan_slug = slug_from_filename(plan_path), falling back to "" when it returns None.** — Unlike review.py/create.py/detail.py which already have the slug seam, launcher lacks it, so a telemetry-wiring step must add the import rather than assume it is present; missing it or letting None reach the recorder mislabels the event. _(when: when a plan-tool step records telemetry from launcher.py and needs a plan slug)_ _(e.g. Step 6 added `from plan_tool.locator import slug_from_filename` to launcher.py alongside the prompt_budget/telemetry module-top imports for record_prompt_budget's plan_slug.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/shell.py:claude_invoke is the SINGLE batch (non-streaming) Claude seam every batch caller funnels through — create (via create.shell_claude_invoker), review/audit (review.shell_review_invoker), detail (detail.shell_detail_invoker), jira (jira.shell_jira_invoker), plus two DIRECT callers lessons.py (phase='lessons_equivalence') and annotate.py. The streaming run path (launcher.run_step) does NOT go through claude_invoke, so anything landed at this seam never touches the run path (and vice versa).** — A pre-send hook, backstop, or measurement placed at claude_invoke automatically covers all batch callers including the two direct ones that have no *_invoker wrapper, but misses the streaming run path entirely; an author who assumes one seam covers 'all Claude calls' either over- or under-scopes. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds pre-send instrumentation/measurement to the batch Claude path or reasons about which callers claude_invoke covers)_ _(e.g. Step 7's total-bytes backstop at claude_invoke covers jira/lessons/annotate (no named-block hook) but deliberately excludes launcher.run_step, which uses the streaming invoker and got its own named-block check in step 6.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **backend.batch_transport(prompt).prompt_bytes (plan_tool/backend.py:PromptTransport.prompt_bytes) is the CANONICAL batch prompt-byte measure — the exact value _run_once returns and _emit_call_end logs as prompt_bytes. It equals len(prompt.encode('utf-8')) for argv-carried backends (claude) but measures the STDIN payload for a stdin-carried backend, so a shell-seam advisory must reuse it (off the backend object already fetched in claude_invoke) rather than recomputing len(encode), or the advisory and the run-log disagree on transport-carried backends.** — The other prompt-budget wiring steps used len(prompt.encode('utf-8')) because their seams are backend-agnostic prompt strings, but the shell seam sits below transport selection where the byte count is transport-dependent; cloning the len(encode) idiom here silently diverges from what the run-log records for a stdin backend. _(when: when a plan-tool step measures prompt size at or below the shell/transport seam)_ _(e.g. Step 7 measured total_bytes = backend.batch_transport(prompt).prompt_bytes, reusing the backend already resolved at the top of claude_invoke; test_backstop_reuses_backend_prompt_bytes pins that a stdin-carried transport measures the stdin payload, not the argv length.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/shell.py already carries thread-scoped ContextVar seams — _active_sink and _active_notifier — set/cleared by external callers and read inside claude_invoke; a new caller-set shell flag must mirror them (a contextvars.ContextVar[bool] defaulting False, a public setter, a read-and-clear consumer), and the thread-scoping is load-bearing because bench's background-thread timeout harness would clobber a plain module global. Tests reset the flag in the autouse _clear_sink_between_tests fixture (extend it) and neutralize shell.record_prompt_budget there so claude_invoke tests don't write real telemetry into the repo.** — An author reaching for a plain global would break under bench's threaded harness and leak the flag across tests; mirroring the existing ContextVar seams gets the correct thread scoping and the established test-hygiene pattern (autouse fixture reset + recorder neutralization) for free. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a caller-set thread-scoped flag or recorder hook to shell.py, or writes hermetic tests around claude_invoke)_ _(e.g. Step 7 added _prompt_budget_advised: ContextVar[bool] + note_prompt_budget_advised() + _consume_prompt_budget_advised(), modeled on _active_sink/_active_notifier, and extended _clear_sink_between_tests to reset it and no-op shell.record_prompt_budget by default.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **BACKLOG.md is a cross-linked graph, not a flat list: an entry id can be referenced from a quality/accuracy roll-up grounding index, a Tn tier line, a 'Remaining …' summary note above a section, and the Risks/Dependencies lines of OTHER entries. Retiring or editing any entry means grepping the whole file for its id and repairing all of those sites, not just its own block.** — An author who edits only the entry's own block leaves the roll-up index, tier line, and sibling-entry dependency lines disagreeing about the entry's status — the same multi-site hazard as CLAUDE.md/RUNBOOK parallel sections, but within one file. _(when: when a plan-tool step edits or removes any BACKLOG.md entry)_ _(e.g. Step 8's #95 lived in five places: its own block under '### A. New capability, well-scoped', the grounding roll-up bullet, the '#95/#97' T3 tier line, the 'Remaining prompt-context quality (#95/#97)' note, and #97's Risks + Dependencies cross-refs.)_

Prompt-inspection/advisory operator docs belong adjacent to the existing 'Inspecting prompts before they run' and 'Mutating vs. read-only modes' sections, and sections end with a '---' separator.** — New RUNBOOK sections are undiscoverable without the ToC bullet, and there's no drift-guard test to catch a missing/mismatched anchor — the gate is an eyeball/anchor-lint pass; anchoring near the sibling prompt sections keeps related operator guidance colocated instead of stranding a new standalone chapter. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a new operator-facing section to RUNBOOK.md)_ _(e.g. Step 8 added 'The prompt-budget advisory' as a top-level ## section right after 'Inspecting prompts before they run', wired its ToC bullet, and closed with the '---' the sibling sections use.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **The `bool(fp) and fp == current` fingerprint-freshness convention is shared-by-copy across plan_tool/cli/review_cmd.py (plan_match), plan_tool/cli/reconcile.py (plan_match / ReconcileFreshness), and inlined in convergence_cmd.py's _actuate_scope_out — an empty fingerprint is 'unverifiable', never a mismatch. Do NOT consolidate convergence's staleness into review/reconcile's plan_match.** — review/reconcile classify a SavedReview's freshness with an additional code_fingerprint axis and their own dataclass; convergence classifies only a plan_fingerprint from RunSnapshot history. Folding them is a cross-module refactor beyond a convergence-side step's footprint and would couple unrelated freshness surfaces. _(when: when a plan-tool step touches fingerprint/staleness freshness in convergence_cmd.py, review_cmd.py, or reconcile.py)_ _(e.g. Step 1 extracted the convergence staleness verdict into a local classify_report_staleness and explicitly deferred consolidating the review/reconcile plan_match rule as a dedicated cross-module change.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **In plan_tool/cli/convergence_cmd.py, _actuate_scope_out is the scope-out actuator (gated on --apply-scope-out); its staleness short-circuit sits AFTER the `rec.fork != FORK_SCOPE_OUT or rec.step_focus is None` early return and BEFORE the seeds_before glob + scope_out_step call, and that ordering is load-bearing.** — The fingerprint read must not move relative to the fork/step_focus check or the seed-glob capture, and the recommend_hint branch keys off the newest fingerprint — a refactor that reorders the read or drops the newest_fp local changes observable hint text/side-effect ordering even while 'looking' behavior-preserving. _(when: when a plan-tool step edits _actuate_scope_out or adds a sibling actuator in convergence_cmd.py)_ _(e.g. Step 1 rewrote _actuate_scope_out to switch on classify_report_staleness's verdict at the same point the fingerprints were computed before, preserving seeds_before, scope_out_step, NarrowError handling, and the recommend_hint branch byte-for-byte.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/detail.py:split_step and plan_tool/scope_out.py:scope_out_step are NOT symmetric executors despite backing sibling convergence actuators: split_step RAISES DetailError (for both pre-mutation refusals — missing target / non-canonical 1..N numbering / unsafe target already-run — and mid-mutation failures) and has NO built-in TTY confirm gate, whereas scope_out_step RETURNS a frozen ScopeOutResult(outcome=applied|recommended|unsafe|empty-plan|step-missing) and owns its own TTY confirm. A convergence actuator dispatching split_step must therefore own the confirm gate and dry-run-first to split refusal (exit 0) from failure (exit non-zero).** — _actuate_split is modeled on _actuate_scope_out, but copying scope-out's 'read the outcome field' and 'let the executor confirm' assumptions would drop the confirm and mis-map exit codes; the two executors' error/result/gate contracts diverge on all three axes. _(when: when a plan-tool step wires split_step or scope_out_step into an actuator, or reasons about their result/exception/gate contracts)_ _(e.g. Step 2 dispatched split_step(path, target_id=rec.step_focus, new_titles=titles, repo_root=ctx.repo_root, author_details=False) behind a caller-owned confirm, using split_step(dry_run=True) as the refusal pre-flight; scope-out needed neither.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/detail.py:split_step with author_details=False is fully deterministic (renumber + depends_on rewire + downstream detail-file migration) and NEVER touches the Claude invoker seam — this is how a dispatching command (convergence, split) stays zero-Claude and always-exit-0 on a completed outcome. It requires new_titles (≥2 distinct non-empty) and offers a dry_run mode that runs every safety check without mutating.** — An author who omits author_details=False (or assumes the split authors the halves inline) breaks the command's zero-Claude / no-@allow_real_claude-marker contract; the two-title minimum and dry_run pre-flight are the load-bearing knobs for a deterministic dispatch. _(when: when a plan-tool step dispatches split_step from a command that must stay zero-Claude / always-exit-0)_ _(e.g. Step 2's _actuate_split calls split_step(..., author_details=False); the applied-split test needs no @allow_real_claude marker and the conftest backend gate proves no Claude was spawned. Authoring the new halves is Deferred to a follow-up `plan-tool detail`.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **In plan_tool/cli/convergence_cmd.py, the two actuation flags (--apply-scope-out, --apply-split) belong in ONE argparse mutually-exclusive group (matching the diagnostic's single-verdict classification — a run forks exactly one way), while any per-actuator input flag (e.g. --into for split titles) sits OUTSIDE that group and is validated at runtime in the actuator, not by argparse.** — Two forks can't be actuated at once, so argparse should reject --apply-scope-out --apply-split before dispatch; but the title input is only required for the split verdict, which is runtime-only, so it can't be argparse-required without breaking scope-out and read-only paths. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a second actuation flag or a per-actuator input flag to convergence_cmd.py)_ _(e.g. Step 2 replaced the standalone --apply-scope-out add with p.add_mutually_exclusive_group() carrying both flags, and added --into (action='append') outside the group with ≥2-distinct-title validation inside _actuate_split.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/convergence_diagnosis.py:render_diagnosis is the single-source human-readable diagnosis block (headline + per-series trend + spinning body + forked remedy command via classify_fork → _split_command/_scope_out_command/_reseed_command). Any surface that shows convergence state must reuse render_diagnosis and gate on the exported VERDICT_SPINNING constant — never inline the "spinning" literal and never re-derive the remedy line — so the report and the `plan-tool convergence` command can't drift.** — The four VERDICT_* constants and the remedy prose already live in one place with a module comment saying downstream keys on the constants; re-deriving the remedy or comparing against a string literal forks the trend/fork wording and reintroduces the drift the single-source design prevents. _(when: when a plan-tool step projects convergence diagnosis state into a report or other surface)_ _(e.g. Step 3's render_convergence_section returns "" unless diagnosis.verdict == VERDICT_SPINNING, then wraps render_diagnosis(diagnosis) output — it re-derives no severity trend or remedy command.)_

A new report section is threaded in as an optional None-default keyword param inserted at its ordered slot; completeness_report is imported only by cli/completeness_phases.py and cli/completeness_cmd.py, so importing convergence_diagnosis at its top is acyclic.** — The section ordering and blank-line spacing are load-bearing conventions a new insertion must match, and the None-default is what preserves byte-for-byte output for existing callers; knowing completeness_report is a near-leaf (only two importers) makes the acyclic-import claim checkable without a graph sweep. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a section to completeness_report.py:build_report_md or imports into completeness_report.py)_ _(e.g. Step 3 placed the spinning-loop section after ## Disposition summary (and ## Halt when present) and before ## Applied this run, keeping the ""-padding convention in the lines list.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **In an iterate completeness loop, plan_tool/cli/completeness_phases.py:write_pre_apply_audit_checkpoint writes a kind="completeness" sidecar for the CURRENT invocation BEFORE the apply loop, and convergence_diagnosis.load_report_history returns one RunSnapshot per on-disk kind="completeness" sidecar (kinds in HISTORY_KINDS) — so by the time _persist_and_present_report runs the final report, this invocation is already present in history as its own checkpoint. Any history/convergence computation added at the final report must dedup that checkpoint against the current run.** — An author who assumes one invocation → one history record double-counts the current run on the iterate path (checkpoint + final) and would mis-fire the spinning verdict; the pre-apply checkpoint write is the load-bearing fact that makes count-once non-trivial here. _(when: when a plan-tool step reads run/report history inside completeness_phases or reasons about how many sidecars one completeness invocation writes)_ _(e.g. Step 4 loaded history = load_report_history(path), appended one in-memory RunSnapshot from sidecar_recs/plan_fp/code_fp, and dropped this invocation's earlier checkpoint so the run is counted once; test_checkpoint_call_passes_no_diagnosis pins that the checkpoint report renders no section.)_

Report-building wiring (new build_report_md kwargs, pre-build computation) goes only inside the fresh-write branch, where path, ctx.repo_root, sidecar_recs, plan_fp, and code_fp are already in scope for the write — reuse those anchors rather than recomputing.** — Wiring placed outside the fresh-write branch either never runs (reuse branch) or duplicates values the write already computed; the sidecar_recs/plan_fp/code_fp locals are exactly the list+fingerprints persisted, so an in-memory current-run snapshot built from them matches what lands on disk for the next run's diagnosis. _(when: when a plan-tool step edits _persist_and_present_report to build or extend the completeness report)_ _(e.g. Step 4 computed the ConvergenceDiagnosis right before the existing build_report_md(...) call inside `if not skip_sidecar_write:`, reusing sidecar_recs/plan_fp/code_fp, and left the skip_sidecar_write reuse branch untouched.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **CLAUDE.md's Architecture section is the registry of cycle-sensitive / stdlib-only leaves — each leaf (backend.py, granularity.py, telemetry.py, convergence_diagnosis.py, …) gets a bold-titled paragraph documenting its import boundary. A plan that lands a NEW leaf owes it the same one-line registration in that style, stating its stdlib-only-below-X boundary and which caller-specific pieces stay injected.** — The import boundary of a leaf is discoverable only from this registry; a new leaf that ships without a paragraph is invisible to a future author who might reintroduce the forbidden edge. The bold-titled-paragraph convention is the established shape to mirror. _(when: when a plan-tool step lands a new cycle-sensitive or stdlib-only leaf module and must document its import boundary)_ _(e.g. Step 4 registered plan_tool/rate_limit_loop.py as a stdlib-only leaf below shell/launcher in a new Architecture paragraph modeled on the neighboring `**Backend abstraction (`backend.py`).**` and `**Decision telemetry (`telemetry.py`).**` registrations.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/scope_out.py's NarrowPreview/NarrowResult fields split by reader: `NarrowResult.renumber`, `NarrowResult.new_current_id`, and `ScopeOutResult.carved_id` are read by plan_tool/cli/scope_out_cmd.py (keep names/types), while carved-id/archive fields are read ONLY by tests/test_scope_out.py — those can generalize to lists freely, the scope_out_cmd-read ones cannot.** — Generalizing the narrow's internal shape is safe only for the test-only fields; touching renumber/new_current_id/ScopeOutResult.carved_id would break the CLI reader. Knowing the exact external-read set scopes a widening refactor to the two in-scope files. _(when: when a plan-tool step edits scope_out.py's NarrowPreview/NarrowResult/ScopeOutResult field shapes)_ _(e.g. Step 1 turned NarrowPreview.carved_id→carved_ids/archive_detail→archive_details and NarrowResult.carved_id→carved_ids/archived→list[Path] but left renumber, new_current_id, and ScopeOutResult.carved_id (scalar) untouched.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **compute_narrow single-sources the old→new id shift map (`old_to_new`) for BOTH the survivor renumber and the depends_on remap; a set-based narrow computes `new_id = s.id - (count of carved ids strictly below s.id)` in that one map — never re-derive the shift in the depends_on repair.** — The single-id form `s.id if s.id < carved else s.id - 1` is just the count-below special case; deriving the shift twice lets the renumber and edge repair drift apart, corrupting the plan graph. _(when: when a plan-tool step edits compute_narrow's renumber or depends_on repair in scope_out.py)_ _(e.g. Step 1 kept one old_to_new map for both the renumber and the depends_on remap; the single-id path reduces to count-below == 0 or 1.)_
- `[cross-step]` **scope_out.py's narrow (compute_narrow/apply_narrow) and plan_tool/detail.py's merge_steps/_apply_step_merge are TWO parallel drop-renumber + depends_on-repair implementations for DIFFERENT operations (carve vs merge); scope_out.py's module docstring cites detail.py for rename hygiene, but consolidating them into one shared renumber primitive is a separate reconcile-only refactor, not in-scope for a scope_out change.** — An author widening the scope-out narrow may be tempted to fold in detail.py's merge renumber to avoid duplication, but the two solve different operations and pulling detail.py into a scope_out step over-scopes it; the duplication is an accepted, docstring-noted follow-up. _(when: when a plan-tool step touches scope_out.py's narrow renumber and considers sharing detail.py's merge renumber)_ _(e.g. Step 1's Deferred explicitly left consolidating the drop-renumber with merge_steps/_apply_step_merge to reconcile.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **apply_narrow's carved-detail archive is order-sensitive against downstream renames: a carved detail whose path is ALSO a downstream rename destination must be archived FIRST (via the carved_is_rename_dest logic) to free the slot, with the rest archived after the renames; the LIFO journal + _rollback carry the extra ('rename'/'restore') entries with no logic change, preserving all-or-nothing on failure.** — Renames refuse on `dst.exists()`; if a carved detail occupying a rename target isn't vacated first, the downstream move collides. The rollback machinery is shape-agnostic and generalizes for free — only the archive-vs-rename ordering is load-bearing. _(when: when a plan-tool step edits apply_narrow's detail archive/rename ordering or rollback in scope_out.py)_ _(e.g. Step 1 split preview.archive_details into rename-destination paths (archived first) vs the rest (after), kept ascending-old-id rename order and the per-rename `dst.exists()` refusal, and relied on the existing LIFO _rollback.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **In plan_tool/scope_out.py, the region (N..M) carve keeps render_carved_seed for the single-id path and adds a separate render_carved_region_seed for >1 id that reuses the SAME block helpers (_scope_block / _done_context_block / _upstream_block), emitting one scope+done block per carved step in ascending id order plus one merged upstream block; scope_out_step branches on region size.** — Reusing the block helpers keeps the region seed's prose vocabulary single-sourced with the single-step seed, and branching (rather than folding a loop into render_carved_seed) keeps the single-step seed bytes identical so its round-trip/block tests pass unmodified. _(when: when a plan-tool step renders a multi-step scope-out seed in scope_out.py)_ _(e.g. Step 2 left render_carved_seed untouched and localized all region prose to render_carved_region_seed, called only when len(carved_ids) > 1.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **scope_out.py's three per-carved-step helpers — _resolve_upstream_context, _resolve_carved_detail_path, _carved_seed_path — must each generalize over the carved set for a region carve; critically, _resolve_upstream_context must DROP any dep that points at another carved id (a carved-on-carved edge is internal to the region, re-planned together) so it never renders as an external prerequisite, and _carved_seed_path must encode the range in the filename to stay collision-safe.** — An in-region dep surfaced as an upstream prerequisite makes the seed read as self-referential; keeping the single-step filename while adding a range suffix (e.g. -carved-<first-slug>-through-<M>.md) keeps region and single-step seeds distinguishable and the -2/-3 collision loop intact. _(when: when a plan-tool step widens scope_out.py's upstream/detail/seed-path helpers from one carved step to a set)_ _(e.g. Step 2 gathered deps of all carved steps, dropped carved-on-carved edges, de-duped, mapped survivors through preview.renumber, and resolved each carved step's detail per-step (pointer-first, canonical fallback, missing flag) keeping the three-case contract.)_
- `[detail-authoring]` **In plan-tool tests, CliRepo.add_plan writes a SINGLE-step plan, so CLI-integration tests that need a multi-step plan (e.g. to drive scope-out --through) must write the multi-step plan file into the repo directly and register it in the manifest, or reuse tests/test_scope_out.py's _register_plan / _scope_out_argv helpers — do not rely on add_plan.** — add_plan can't produce the multi-step fixture a range carve requires, and the new --through CLI-integration tests live in a new tests/cli/test_scope_out_cmd.py marked @pytest.mark.integration (driving main([...])) while the existing single-step TestScopeOutCLI stays in tests/test_scope_out.py. _(when: when a plan-tool CLI-integration test needs a multi-step plan fixture)_ _(e.g. Step 2 added tests/cli/test_scope_out_cmd.py driving main through parse→dispatch→command for the range flag, seeding a multi-step plan via _register_plan rather than CliRepo.add_plan.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **For scope-out, contiguity and range validity are CLI concerns owned by plan_tool/cli/scope_out_cmd.py:cmd_scope_out — it expands --step N/--through M into list(range(N, M+1)), rejects M<N with rc 2 before scope_out_step is called, and passes any subset down; scope_out.py/compute_narrow accept an arbitrary id set (step 1) and add no contiguity or out-of-order check.** — The narrow was generalized to any subset, so the contiguity contract can only be enforced at the one range-expansion site; scope_out_step never sees an invalid range, and convergence_cmd.py:cmd_convergence (single rec.step_focus) and split_criteria.py (single step.id) remain the only other, single-id callers. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds or reasons about range/contiguity validation for scope-out)_ _(e.g. Step 2 put the range→set expansion and out-of-order rc 2 in cmd_scope_out and left convergence_diagnosis.py:_scope_out_command's --through rendering + convergence --apply-scope-out actuation to step 3.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/cli/review_cmd.py builds _build_review_action_fn at THREE sites — two in cmd_review (the reuse path and the fresh-walk path) and one in cmd_review_walk — and each reads its opt-in flags via `getattr(args, "<dest>", False)` because the reuse/fresh-walk builders are reached from a namespace that may not carry the attr; a new builder opt-in must be threaded into all three with the same getattr-default idiom.** — Missing one of the three sites silently disables the flag on that lane, and reading the attr directly (not via getattr-default) can AttributeError on the reuse/fresh-walk namespace that omits it. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds an opt-in threaded into _build_review_action_fn in review_cmd.py)_ _(e.g. Step 4 threaded allow_merge_remedy=getattr(args,'merge_remedy',False) / allow_reground_remedy=getattr(args,'reground_remedy',False) alongside the existing allow_structural_remedy=getattr(args,'apply_structural',False) at all three call sites.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **In the reconcile walk, the re-ground directive is info-level and hidden unless `--include-info` is passed, whereas a merge directive is visible without it; a re-ground apply opt-in (`--reground`/`--apply-structural`) changes what happens on APPLY, not visibility — so its help/docs must say it still needs --include-info to surface the finding, and it must not be mistaken for a visibility toggle.** — An operator passing only --reground sees nothing happen because the finding was never surfaced; the apply gate and the visibility gate are independent, and conflating them makes the flag read as broken. _(when: when a plan-tool step touches re-ground directive visibility or a reground apply opt-in in the reconcile walk)_ _(e.g. Step 4's --reground help states the --include-info dependency and its recommend-only message names the granular flag beside --apply-structural.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **docs/cli/reconcile-plan.md and docs/cli/reconcile-plan-walk.md are generated from the argparse parser by `python -m plan_tool.cli_reference --write` and drift-guarded by tests/cli/test_cli_reference.py; a flag added to p_review / p_review_walk in review_cmd.py requires regenerating both, and that test doubles as the CLI-wiring check for the new flag.** — These two files are never hand-edited; the drift test red-until-regenerated is the honest signal that the flag landed in argparse, so the regen is load-bearing, not cosmetic. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a flag to the reconcile-plan / reconcile-plan-walk subparsers)_ _(e.g. Step 4 added --merge/--reground to both parsers, regenerated the two docs, and used a green test_cli_reference.py as the wiring gate.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/reground.py is a leaf that may import only locator / parser / schema — pinned by test_imports_neither_launcher_nor_detail_at_module_level, which greps the WHOLE source for any plan_tool.detail / plan_tool.launcher import. - `[domain-shape]` **A create --from-existing re-baseline/carve seed rendered inside a leaf (reground.py) must render flagged steps from Step FRONTMATTER only (title, all_files, change type, status, scope, features) — never per-step detail bodies — because resolving detail files needs plan_tool.detail helpers the leaf cannot import; this is also correct in spirit since a re-baseline re-decomposes from current code, not stale detail prose.** — render_carved_seed embeds a carved step's detail body, but that path is unavailable to a leaf; frontmatter is sufficient for 'these are built, don't re-plan them' done-context, and detail-body enrichment is a deferred caller-injects-it follow-up. _(when: when a plan-tool leaf module must render a create --from-existing seed for a set of steps)_ _(e.g. Step 5's render_rebaseline_seed lists flagged steps' id/title/files from Step frontmatter under an 'already implemented — do not re-plan' framing and defers detail-body embedding.)_
- `[cross-step]` **plan-tool now has THREE parallel create --from-existing seed renderers that deliberately mirror (not share) one shape: scope_out.render_carved_seed, annotate_render.render_create_seed, and reground.render_rebaseline_seed. Consolidating them into one shared leaf is a reconcile-owned refactor, not in scope for a step that adds/edits one of them.** — The mirror-not-share choice is forced by differing import boundaries (reground can't import detail; scope_out can); an author tempted to extract a common renderer would either re-introduce a forbidden edge or over-scope the step. _(when: when a plan-tool step touches one of the create --from-existing seed renderers and considers deduplicating them)_ _(e.g. Step 5's Deferred listed 'consolidate the three seed renderers' as reconcile-owned, noting scope_out already mirrors annotate_render without importing it.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **When a plan ships structural-remedy arms, the durable prose describing those surfaces lives in three specific CLAUDE.md Architecture paragraphs — 'Structural remedy vocabulary', 'Granularity advisor', 'Convergence diagnostic' — AND RUNBOOK.md's 'four structural remedies, as one model' block, the scope-out walkthrough, the convergence FORK_SCOPE_OUT walkthrough, and the walk-dispatch 'Structural-directive findings' item; a docs-refresh must sweep all of them, not just BACKLOG.md.** — These paragraphs each restate the pre-arm mechanism (single-step scope-out, --apply-structural umbrella only, mark-done-only re-ground), so shipping the range carve / per-remedy flags / re-baseline disposition leaves every one stale; missing any makes the docs assert an arm is unbuilt and the next reconcile audit flags drift. _(when: when a plan-tool step reconciles docs after shipping a scope-out / merge / re-ground / convergence structural-remedy arm)_ _(e.g. Step 7 updated CLAUDE.md's scope-out bullet ('prints plan-tool scope-out <name> --step N' → also --through M), the FORK_SCOPE_OUT clause, and the Granularity-advisor merge/re-ground gating, plus RUNBOOK.md's four-remedies model and scope-out example block (adding --step 2 --through 4).)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/review.py:heuristic_already_done iterates `step.files` (NOT step.all_files) and stores the exact declared string in HeuristicHit.file (`file=f`); so a HeuristicHit's file is string-equal to its Step.files entry, and any detector correlating hits to declared files matches against step.files with a plain set comparison and no path normalization.** — step.all_files folds in `creates` paths the heuristic never scans, so comparing hits against all_files would flag a never-scanned `creates` path as an 'un-built declared file' — a false trigger; and adding normalization diverges from the heuristic's exact-string storage. _(when: when a plan-tool detector correlates heuristic_already_done hits with a step's declared files)_ _(e.g. _code_reveals_split_recommendations counts distinct HeuristicHit.file values and looks for a step.files entry with no hit, all via bare set ops against step.files.)_

- `[cross-step]` **plan_tool/review_walk.py:split_escalation_target gates auto-dispatch to escalate_to_split on BOTH rec.severity == 'medium' AND the source being in extra_apply_sources; therefore an `info`-severity granularity-split rec is inherently recommend-only and never auto-dispatched, so reusing the shared `granularity-split` literal at info is safe — no separate token or routing carve-out is needed to keep it advisory.** — The severity==medium clause is the auto-dispatch guard; an info finding satisfying is_structural (routes through triage_reason's split branch) still can't reach escalate_to_split, so info + granularity-split is the correct advisory shape without inventing a new source. _(when: when a plan-tool step emits a granularity-split (or other structural) finding and must decide whether it can be auto-dispatched)_ _(e.g. test_info_code_split_not_auto_dispatched asserts split_escalation_target returns False for an info granularity-split rec even with granularity-split in extra_apply_sources.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **BACKLOG.md carries three forward-pointing priority-steering surfaces that name the single highest OPEN concrete item — the per-tier bullet (e.g. `- **T2 — …:**`), the Readiness-lens Concrete bullet's 'Highest open by tier' chain, and the 'Next concrete pick' line — so retiring the item they name requires re-pointing all three at its successor (and keeping the two 'next' surfaces agreeing), not just striking the mention. This is in addition to the by-#ID lens roll-ups.** — These three read as prose that steers an operator's next action; unlike a member enumeration, they assert a ranking, so removing the top item leaves a hole that must be filled by the next-ranked item — and the tier bullet's header (which names the machinery the retired item owned) stays while only its item list changes. _(when: when a plan-tool step retires a BACKLOG.md entry/arm that is currently the highest open concrete item in a tier)_ _(e.g. Step 3 dropped #70 from the T2 bullet (leaving #71 as its only open item), removed the #70 lead from the 'Highest open by tier' chain (now starting at #72/#97), and rewrote 'Next concrete pick' to name #72 — three separate priority surfaces beyond the #ID lens roll-ups.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **BACKLOG.md entries cite each other's arms as origins by #ID+arm phrase (e.g. #103 and #106 cite '#70 arm 4' as the origin of the completeness-apply split bridge; a structural-observation ledger entry cites '#70 auto-bridge work' as design context). These origin citations point at ALREADY-SHIPPED arms and must survive a whole-entry deletion of the cited entry.** — An author deleting #70 in full may assume `grep '#70'` returning zero is the success condition, but that would scrub accurate provenance from live entries; the correct post-delete state is 'no line frames #70 as OPEN work,' with shipped-arm origin citations intact. _(when: when a plan-tool step deletes a BACKLOG.md entry whose earlier (shipped) arms are cited as origins by other live entries)_ _(e.g. Step 3's acceptance criteria explicitly required the #103/#106 '#70 arm 4' origin references to STAY after the #70 entry block was removed; the deletion gate was 'no line asserts #70 has open work,' not 'no #70 mention exists.')_

The doc edit is the mandatory gate; the code edit is a no-op.** — An author expecting to register new fields in data_contract.py wastes effort, while one who forgets the DATA_CONTRACT.md edit leaves the drift test red; the guard's dynamic discovery inverts where the required change lives. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds or removes fields on a dataclass registered in data_contract.py's PersistedDataclassContract)_ _(e.g. Step 1 added four DecisionEvent fields, made only DATA_CONTRACT.md edits (+ the schema_version '1'→'2' prose), and confirmed the registry auto-documented the fields with no data_contract.py change.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/telemetry.py is a stdlib-only leaf (grep -E '^(from|import) plan_tool' stays empty): any digest/fingerprint it stores must be CALLER-SUPPLIED already-computed values, never computed inside telemetry — it must not import review_persistence or fingerprint. New primitives it needs must be stdlib (hashlib, contextvars, contextlib).** — Importing the fingerprint producers to compute digests in-leaf re-introduces the first-party edge the leaf forbids; the record-observes-not-computes contract keeps telemetry recordable from any module without a cycle. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds fields or logic to telemetry.py that could tempt importing a first-party digest/fingerprint producer)_ _(e.g. record_decision accepts plan_fingerprint: str and code_fingerprint: Optional[dict] as caller args (stored as dict(code_fingerprint or {})) and computes decision_id with hashlib only.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/telemetry.py:record_decision is the SOLE writer of decisions.jsonl, and all 8 wrapper recorders funnel through it; enriching record_decision with new DEFAULTED params is enough to add fields to every event, and the wrappers (and their tests) stay byte-unchanged until a later step forwards the new args.** — The single-choke-point shape lets a schema-enrichment step touch exactly one function plus the dataclass and reader — an author who plans to edit each wrapper over-scopes the step, and a non-defaulted param would break all 8 wrappers at once. _(when: when a plan-tool step enriches the telemetry decision event schema or record_decision's signature)_ _(e.g. Step 1 stamped decision_id/run_id/fingerprints inside record_decision with defaulted params, explicitly deferring wrapper forwarding to step 2 and asserting the 8 wrappers pass with no edits.)_
- `[cross-step]` **During a multi-step field-promotion migration in plan_tool telemetry (a value moving from a wrapper's context/open-bag into a first-class base-event field), the intermediate step legitimately keeps the value in BOTH places — the new defaulted base field AND the wrapper's context plus its registered_open_bag_keys entry — and must NOT remove the open-bag registration until the dedicated promotion step.** — Removing the open-bag registration in the field-adding step orphans the wrapper that still writes the key into context, tripping the open-bag drift guard; the dual existence is correct until the promotion step rewrites the wrapper. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a first-class field that a later step will promote out of an existing context/open-bag, leaving the value temporarily in both)_ _(e.g. plan_fingerprint/code_fingerprint became defaulted base fields in step 1 but stayed registered as context keys of record_plan_criteria_breakdown; step 2 owns promoting them out and deleting the registered_open_bag_keys entries.)_

- `[cross-step]` **The PROMOTION step that completes a plan_tool telemetry field migration must land THREE edits atomically: (1) stop the wrapper writing the key into `context`, (2) remove the key from `plan_tool/data_contract.py:registered_open_bag_keys()`'s `("DecisionEvent","context")` frozenset, and (3) remove its row from the DATA_CONTRACT.md context-key table — none can lag, because registered_open_bag_keys() feeds registry_fingerprint() AND the ## Input-section validator check_input_contract_references, so a lingering registration describes a context key the code no longer writes.** — This is the completion half of the 'keep the value in both places until the promotion step' rule: once the wrapper stops writing the key, the open-bag registration and the doc are stale claims about context contents, and the registration drives a fingerprint + a reference validator that must track reality. _(when: when a plan_tool telemetry step promotes a key out of a wrapper's context/open-bag into a base DecisionEvent field (the dedicated promotion step))_ _(e.g. Step 2 stopped record_plan_criteria_breakdown writing plan_fingerprint/code_fingerprint into context, dropped both from registered_open_bag_keys()'s ("DecisionEvent","context") set, and removed their rows from DATA_CONTRACT.md's Plan split-criteria breakdown Context keys table — all in one change.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **In plan_tool telemetry, forwarding a scope field into record_decision's decision_id hash is per-wrapper: record_create_step_outcome forwards its single step_id (and KEEPS the additive context["step_id"] write), while record_code_reveals_split holds plural step_ids and leaves record_decision's step_id unset because the hash's step_id input is a single optional string.** — The decision_id hash takes one optional step_id; a wrapper with a plural step set has no single focus to fold in, so uniformly wiring step_id across all 8 wrappers would mis-map the plural case. The context write stays even after the hash-forward — the forward is additive, not a move. _(when: when a plan_tool telemetry step forwards step_id into the decision_id hash across the 8 recorder wrappers)_ _(e.g. Step 2 added record_decision(..., step_id=step_id) to record_create_step_outcome while leaving record_code_reveals_split's step_id argument unpassed.)_
