- `[domain-shape]` **BACKLOG.md #72 is a PHASED entry (phase 1 recorder shipped earlier; this plan shipped the outcome-linkage join-key schema; the resolver / `plan-tool telemetry` analysis-and-recommend surface, outcome-verdict derivation, and decision-site key backfill remain phase 2–3) and is cited as an origin/future-analysis-surface by #97, #117, #74, and #82. A plan that ships one of its phases updates #72's Status/Remaining and keeps it OPEN — it does not retire #72, re-point the priority roll-ups, or touch those four cross-citations.** — An author who saw the #70/#101 whole-entry-retirement lessons may treat any BACKLOG bookkeeping step as a retirement; #72's phased shape means shipping a slice is a partial update, and its downstream citations reference the still-unshipped phase 2–3 and must survive. _(when: when a plan-tool step ships a phase/slice of BACKLOG #72 (decision/outcome telemetry) or reasons about which of its references change)_ _(e.g. Step 4 rewrote #72's Status to credit the schema slice (pointing at docs/implementation-plans/2-telemetry-linkage-schema.md), narrowed Remaining to resolver/analysis-surface/backfill, and left the T3/Highest-open/Next-pick pointers and the #97/#117/#74/#82 citations in place.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **In plan_tool/rate_limit_loop.py, a transient-only seam belongs inside the `if will_retry_transient:` block BEFORE the delay/notify/sleep; `on_nonsuccess` fires earlier in the iteration with `will_retry_transient` as its transient-budget PREDICTION and must NOT be re-threaded with a later STOP decision — doing so would change shell's canary-then-raw-nonzero surface ordering that steps 2/3 depend on. A STOP arm returns the attempt's (rc, payload) terminally without incrementing transient_attempts/current_attempt.** — on_nonsuccess and the transient guard are two distinct decision points in the same iteration; conflating them (flipping on_nonsuccess retroactively, or consulting the guard outside the will_retry_transient block) either changes shell's observable notifier ordering or gates the guard on non-transient arms — divergences that only manifest under a live rate limit / transient. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a transient-only seam or decision to run_with_rate_limit_recovery's TRANSIENT arm)_ _(e.g. Step 1 consulted retry_guard only in the will_retry_transient block, left on_nonsuccess and its predictive will_retry untouched (shell wires always-retry so never reaches STOP; launcher's on_nonsuccess is empty), and the STOP branch returns terminal without touching the attempt counters.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **After BACKLOG #101, run_with_rate_limit_recovery is the SINGLE home for transient-retry control flow — shell.claude_invoke and launcher.shell_invoker carry no separate transient arm (their only reference to the loop is the one `run_with_rate_limit_recovery(` call site). A new transient-arm behavior is added once in the leaf; there is no duplicate branch in the callers to also change, and a default no-op seam keeps both un-wired callers byte-identical.** — An author may assume the pre-#101 two-copy world and hunt for a second transient arm in shell/launcher to edit; there is none, so the change is confined to the leaf plus a per-caller seam wire, and defaulting the seam preserves both callers until their wiring steps land. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds or edits transient-retry behavior and needs to know how many homes/callers must change)_ _(e.g. Step 1 added the retry_guard branch only in rate_limit_loop.py; shell and launcher reference the loop solely at their `run_with_rate_limit_recovery(` call, and the ALWAYS_RETRY default kept both byte-identical pending steps 2/3.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/launcher.py:_git_changed_paths(cwd) runs `git status --porcelain -z --untracked-files=all` and returns the repo-relative changed-path SET, with two load-bearing contracts: gitignored paths are excluded (porcelain omits them, so run-log / .plan-tool/telemetry writes never appear), and a non-git tree or ANY git error returns the EMPTY set. Reuse it for any git changed-state snapshot/delta — do not re-parse porcelain.** — Its ignored-exclusion means a guard keying on the changed set can't false-trigger on tool-owned writes, and its empty-on-error means the guard degrades to the safe default off-repo for free; a fresh parser diverges from both and needs its own error handling. _(when: when a plan-tool step needs a git working-tree changed-path snapshot or delta)_ _(e.g. Step 2's shell_invoker guard captures baseline=_git_changed_paths(spawn_cwd) and re-reads it per transient attempt, relying on ignored-exclusion (no telemetry false-trigger) and empty-on-error (inert off-repo).)_
- `[domain-shape]` **In launcher/run, the repo root for a spawned Claude turn is reached via plan_tool/backend.py:get_active_spawn_cwd() (returns the spawn cwd or None), NOT a parameter — the Invoker protocol carries only the prompt. A per-spawn git/repo decision computed caller-side reads get_active_spawn_cwd() and treats None (tests, direct callers, non-run paths) as 'inert/degrade to default', mirroring how repo_root already reaches the spawn sites.** — Widening Invoker to carry repo_root would break every caller and the minimal-prompt contract; get_active_spawn_cwd() already resolves per-spawn, and its None case is the correct signal that no repo context exists so the caller-side decision should be a no-op. _(when: when a plan-tool step needs the spawned turn's repo root / cwd for a caller-side decision in launcher)_ _(e.g. Step 2's shell_invoker snapshots git state only when get_active_spawn_cwd() is a real path and passes step 1's always-retry singleton (inert) when it returns None.)_
- `[cross-step]` **run_step ALREADY snapshots a git baseline via _git_changed_paths for the TEST-AUTHORING gate (git_test_baseline); a new per-invoke guard that also snapshots git state (e.g. shell_invoker's partial-mutation baseline) is a SEPARATE baseline for a different gate at a different altitude — do not fold them together. Each gate owns its own snapshot point.** — The two baselines answer different questions (did the step author a test? vs did this transient attempt mutate the tree?) and are captured at different frames (run_step vs shell_invoker entry); conflating them would mis-scope one gate's delta onto the other's inputs. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a git-state baseline in the launcher run path and another gate already snapshots git state)_ _(e.g. Step 2 kept shell_invoker's partial-mutation baseline distinct from run_step's git_test_baseline, noting the test-gate baseline is out of scope.)_
- `[cross-step]` **The batch/streaming split for a git-state guard on the Claude-invoke path: the streaming decider lives in plan_tool/launcher.py:shell_invoker (real git delta), while the batch counterpart plan_tool/cli/gitcommit.py:working_tree_dirty is wired to a constant no-op because proposal/batch turns don't mutate the tree — a streaming-path guard step must NOT touch working_tree_dirty or the batch wiring (that's the batch-caller step's concern).** — shell_invoker (streaming) and shell.claude_invoke (batch) are the two homes of the recovery loop; a git-mutation guard is meaningful only on the streaming path that spawns editing turns, so the batch path takes an always-retry constant. Reaching into working_tree_dirty from the streaming step over-scopes it. _(when: when a plan-tool step wires a git-state retry guard on one of the two rate-limit-loop callers (streaming vs batch))_ _(e.g. Step 2 (streaming) computed the delta in shell_invoker and explicitly left gitcommit.py:working_tree_dirty / the batch always-retry wiring to step 3.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/shell.py:claude_invoke is a PERMANENT opt-out of the retry_guard seam (batch/proposal turns never mutate the working tree), and it passes rate_limit_loop's always-retry singleton EXPLICITLY into run_with_rate_limit_recovery — not by relying on the default — so the opt-out is visible at the call site; extend the existing `from plan_tool.rate_limit_loop import (...)` block for the singleton rather than adding a second import line.** — The streaming counterpart (launcher.shell_invoker) owns the real git-delta guard; shell's batch path can't double-apply partial edits, so it will never wire a real guard. Passing the constant explicitly distinguishes 'deliberately never stops a transient' from 'forgot to wire', and reusing the existing leaf import keeps the module's import surface unchanged. _(when: when a plan-tool step wires the batch shell.claude_invoke caller of run_with_rate_limit_recovery or reasons about its retry-guard stance)_ _(e.g. Step 3 added only retry_guard=<always-retry singleton> to the run_with_rate_limit_recovery(...) call inside the ExitStack block, left every wrapper-owned piece (shutil.which guard, _maybe_warn_shell_prompt_budget, resolve_on_rate_limit_policy, _rate_limit_backend_scope, on_nonsuccess canary+raw-nonzero) untouched, and added no git/spawn-cwd read.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **When a plan spawned from a BUG_BACKLOG.md `## RISK` entry ships only a PARTIAL fix (a correctness-now response that closes the corruption, with a resilience follow-up deferred), the closing step DELETES the RISK entry in full — the section heading stays and reads `_(none outstanding)_` when it was the sole entry — and routes the deferred remainder to BACKLOG.md as a new forward-looking entry, NOT a slimmed RISK stub. Once response A closes the corruption there is no live wrong-behavior bug; the follow-up is forward work.** — BUG_BACKLOG = things the code does wrong NOW; BACKLOG = forward-looking work (CLAUDE.md's decision rule). Leaving a trimmed RISK stub for the deferred resilience work wrongly asserts an outstanding bug, and deleting the heading loses the section's `_(none outstanding)_` placeholder convention. _(when: when a plan-tool step closes a BUG_BACKLOG RISK by shipping a partial fix whose remainder is deferred)_ _(e.g. Step 4 deleted the `Transient retry re-drives the acceptEdits streaming run over a partially-mutated tree` RISK (A closed the corruption), left `## RISK` reading `_(none outstanding)_`, and filed response B (snapshot-restore) as a new BACKLOG.md entry under `### A. New capability, well-scoped`.)_
- `[create-heuristic]` **The docs/bookkeeping tail step of a plan that partially fixes a BUG_BACKLOG RISK (ship-now + deferred-remainder) must list BOTH BUG_BACKLOG.md (to close the shipped RISK) and BACKLOG.md (to file the deferred remainder) in its files — one file is not enough because the close and the follow-up land in different backlogs.** — A single-backlog file list either leaves the RISK asserting a live bug (missing BUG_BACKLOG.md) or drops the deferred resilience work (missing BACKLOG.md); the two-backlog split is intrinsic to a partial-fix plan's closing step. _(when: when create decomposes a BUG_BACKLOG-derived fix into a shipped response plus a deferred remainder and proposes the closing/bookkeeping step)_ _(e.g. create proposed step 4's files as docs/RUN_FLOW.md, RUNBOOK.md, BUG_BACKLOG.md, AND BACKLOG.md — correctly carrying both backlog files for the close-plus-file-remainder pair.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **Per-site fingerprint-carry policy for plan-tool decision telemetry: carry plan_fingerprint EVERYWHERE (cheap renumber-proof anchor from review_persistence.compute_plan_fingerprint(path)); carry the full code_fingerprint map (fingerprint.compute_code_fingerprint(plan, path, repo_root)) ONLY where the decision is about code state OR the module already parses a Plan cheaply — never parse a Plan just to fill code_fingerprint.** — code_fingerprint needs a parsed Plan; adding it at a site that only resolves a path (like convergence, whose verdict is about saved-report recurrence not code state) means parsing a Plan the decision doesn't need — plan_fingerprint alone is the correct carry there and code_fingerprint stays {}. _(when: when a plan-tool step wires plan/code fingerprints into a decision-telemetry recorder call site)_ _(e.g. record_code_reveals_split / record_granularity / record_audit_coverage carry both; record_convergence in cmd_convergence carries plan_fingerprint only (no parsed Plan, code_fingerprint == {}).)_

The other caller, collect_deterministic_findings, passes reconcile_lane=False + heuristic_hits=[] so the code-grounded producer never fires — leave its call at the default and it records nothing.** — The split recorder fires inside extract_recommendations but the function was never given the path the fingerprint helpers need; the additive optional param keeps the non-reconcile caller byte-unchanged (its producer is already gated off) while review_plan_full supplies the real path. _(when: when a plan-tool step enriches a producer inside review.py:extract_recommendations that needs the plan's on-disk path)_ _(e.g. Step 1 added plan_path: Optional[Path] = None to extract_recommendations, threaded it from review_plan_full, and computed fingerprints inside the existing reconcile-lane `if split_recs:` block guarded on plan_path is not None.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/cli/completeness_phases.py's sidecar-persist tail ALREADY computes compute_plan_fingerprint(path) and compute_code_fingerprint(plan, path, ctx.repo_root) together; a new fingerprint-carrying site in that module (or a sibling CLI phase) should mirror that exact compute shape and its body-local import style rather than inventing a new pattern — but treat it as a separate computation (it exists for report staleness), not something to consolidate in a telemetry-backfill step.** — The shape (both helpers, from plan/path/ctx.repo_root, lazily imported next to the telemetry import) is already proven at that site; mirroring it keeps the new carry consistent, while folding the two computations together over-scopes a backfill step into a refactor. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a fingerprint compute inside completeness_phases.py or a sibling CLI phase module)_ _(e.g. record_granularity/record_audit_coverage backfills reused the sidecar tail's compute_plan_fingerprint + compute_code_fingerprint calls and body-local imports; consolidating with the staleness compute was explicitly deferred.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/create.py's _review_step_change_types (the confirm/override/split gate) runs BEFORE write_new_plan, so at create-decision time the plan markdown is not on disk: review_persistence.compute_plan_fingerprint returns the stable empty-file digest (non-empty but identical for every fresh create — not a join key), while fingerprint.compute_code_fingerprint over step.files/creates is the meaningful create-time anchor. - `[domain-shape]` **A plan_tool telemetry recorder may emit `context` keys that are NOT in data_contract.py:registered_open_bag_keys() — registration gates only the `## Input` prose-reference validator (check_input_contract_references) and registry_fingerprint, not what a recorder is allowed to write. So a brand-new recorder family that adds context keys touches NO data_contract.py; registration is required only when a `## Input` section cross-references the key.** — The 'promotion step must remove open-bag registration' lessons can be mis-read as 'every context key must be registered'; the inverse is true for a fresh recorder — record_convergence already emits `verdict`/`runs` unregistered, so a new recorder's context keys are free unless prose references them. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a new telemetry recorder or new context keys and is deciding whether data_contract.py:registered_open_bag_keys() needs an edit)_ _(e.g. record_apply_verdict emits context={'verdict': ..., 'step_id': ...} with no registered_open_bag_keys entry, mirroring record_convergence's unregistered `verdict`/`runs`; the step's file set correctly excludes data_contract.py.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/launcher.py:parse_apply_verdict returns one of APPLIED / NOT-APPLICABLE / BLOCKED / BLOCKED-STRUCTURAL or None, and its sole consumer in apply_finding normalizes None→'UNKNOWN'; parse_deep_verdict is a SEPARATE token set for the deep-verify flow. A step recording or reasoning about the apply verdict reads parse_apply_verdict's output only and must not re-derive/re-classify the token — the classification lives solely in parse_apply_verdict.** — Knowing the exact five-value normalized vocabulary (four tokens plus UNKNOWN) and that parse_deep_verdict is out of scope prevents re-implementing the classifier or conflating the two verdict flows. _(when: when a plan-tool step reads or records the apply-finding verdict, or reasons about parse_apply_verdict vs parse_deep_verdict)_ _(e.g. record_apply_verdict's context['verdict'] ranges over {APPLIED, NOT-APPLICABLE, BLOCKED, BLOCKED-STRUCTURAL, UNKNOWN}; the step explicitly grep-confirmed parse_deep_verdict is a distinct sibling and left it untouched.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/launcher.py:escalate_to_split returns a frozen EscalateResult whose outcome is one of applied/recommended/unsafe/proposal-unusable/step-missing (only applied mutates), and it is reached only from detail.py:generate_detail (convergence loop) and cli/review_actions.py:_dispatch_structural_escalation — never from a `run`. So a telemetry recorder added inside it sees _active_run_id UNSET (run_id defaults to '') with no threading needed, and its fingerprint snapshot must be hoisted above the applied arm's write_plan so all five arms capture the PRE-split code state the bridge observed.** — Knowing the caller set (no run path) means run_id needs no wiring; knowing the applied arm mutates the plan file means an un-hoisted code_fingerprint would capture post-split bytes on that one arm, diverging from the other four. - `[domain-shape]` **For a telemetry family whose event has a FIXED decision semantic but a VARYING result value, mirror plan_tool/telemetry.py:record_convergence — set the `decision` constant to a single fixed literal and put the varying value in `context` — rather than encoding the varying value as the `decision`. record_convergence uses a fixed decision with `verdict` in context; a new outcome-recording family (e.g. escalate-split) uses ESCALATE_SPLIT_DECISION='resolved' with the varying `outcome` string in context.** — The decision field partitions the family into semantic buckets; a per-outcome decision would fragment one conceptual decision-family across many decision literals and diverge from the sibling convergence recorder, which is the established template for fixed-decision/varying-result events. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a telemetry recorder whose event has one decision meaning but a varying result/verdict/outcome value)_ _(e.g. Step 5 set ESCALATE_SPLIT_DECISION='resolved' and carried EscalateResult.outcome in context['outcome'], explicitly mirroring record_convergence's verdict-in-context shape rather than record_create_step_outcome's per-outcome decision.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **A new plan_tool/prompts/*.md prompt that expects JSON output is modeled on plan_tool/prompts/distill-seed.md (JSON-only, "first character `{`, last `}`", evidence-only framing); its rendering stays in the CALLER module via a function-local `from plan_tool.renderer import prompts_dir` + string.Template().safe_substitute(${name}) — do NOT edit renderer.py, which is not the prompt-owner's file.** — renderer.py owns only the prompts_dir resolver, not per-prompt render logic; keeping the render inline (as detail.py:render_detail_prompt does) means a prompt-adding step touches only its own module + the .md file, and matches the ${name}/safe_substitute convention already used across the codebase. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a new JSON-output prompt file and needs to render it)_ _(e.g. Step 2 wrote prompts/concept-emit.md (JSON-only, depth/breadth-bounded, ${evidence}/${plan_title} placeholders) and rendered it inside concept_tree.py; renderer.py was not in the step's files and stayed untouched.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **The `invoker=` producer seam for a Claude round-trip must route through plan_tool/shell.py:claude_invoke (never a bare subprocess) — that call site alone earns the shared backend-selection, rate-limit-recovery loop, AND the _maybe_warn_shell_prompt_budget backstop, and it is what makes tests/conftest.py's real-backend gate cover the seam. A producer that shelled out directly would bypass all four and the gate.** — claude_invoke is the single chokepoint that carries backend/rate-limit/prompt-budget behavior; routing the default invoker through it means the new producer inherits every recovery path and the conftest guard with zero new code, and skipping it silently drops all of them. _(when: when a plan-tool step wires the default invoker for a new Claude round-trip seam)_ _(e.g. Step 2's shell_concept_invoker does a function-local `from plan_tool.shell import claude_invoke`; the detail cites that this is why the seam must never use subprocess and why no conftest change is needed.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan-tool's interactive-walk building blocks live at three deliberately-separate sites: create.py's `_review_step_change_types`/`_ask_change_type` (the `_SPLIT` sentinel that flags a structural action inside a numbered-choice loop), create.py's `_ask_int_list`/`_ask_choice`/`_ask_yn` input primitives, and scope_out.py's `_confirm_scope_out` (the `yes → non-TTY → interactive` gate idiom). A stdlib-only leaf that needs an interactive walk must REIMPLEMENT these locally (a fresh sentinel mirroring `_SPLIT`, its own ~10-line int-list/choice/yn helpers, its own gate) — importing them from create.py/scope_out.py would reintroduce the first-party edge the leaf forbids; consolidation is reconcile-owned.** — The three sites are the canonical templates for the walk/gate/input shape, but they sit in orchestrator modules a leaf can't import; the codebase's mirror-not-share convention (already applied to its three seed renderers and its input helpers) means a leaf re-derives the small helpers rather than sharing them, keeping `grep -E '^(from|import) plan_tool' <leaf>` empty. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds an interactive walk, structural-action sentinel, or int-list/choice/yes-no prompt to a stdlib-only leaf)_ _(e.g. Step 3's navigate_concepts generalized `_SPLIT`→`_DRILL` for its level stack, re-derived the int-list/choice/yn validation locally, and followed _confirm_scope_out's gate — all inside concept_tree.py with every first-party import kept function-local; consolidating the input helpers was listed under Deferred as reconcile-owned.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/create.py:_render_plan_body picks each section body with precedence synthesized_sections (canonical keys) ≻ seed_sections ≻ _(TODO)_; to make a new source win over BOTH the distill pass and the body-synthesis round-trip, overwrite that canonical key inside the synthesized_sections dict AFTER propose_body_sections runs and BEFORE _find_placeholder_body_sections / write_new_plan — no new precedence tier or write_new_plan arg is needed.** — synthesized_sections is the top precedence source and the same dict write_new_plan reads, so an overwrite there is the single seam that beats every other section producer without touching the renderer signature. _(when: when a plan-tool step needs a value to override create's synthesized/distilled body section)_ _(e.g. Step 4 overwrote synthesized_sections['Deferred']/['Out of scope'] from the concept tree between propose_body_sections and the fail-loud TODO check.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/create.py's _canonical_body_section_keys() fixes exactly 8 distill section keys (including 'Out of scope' and 'Deferred'), and _validate_distilled_sections requires all 8 present with null allowed. Any edit to distill-seed.md that stops the distill pass guessing a section must keep all 8 keys and have it emit null — dropping a key fails the validator; the single-plan shape must stay 8-key.** — The distill validator counts keys, not values, so 'don't guess this' is expressed as emit-null, never omit; a dropped key reds the distill unit tests. _(when: when a plan-tool step edits distill-seed.md's per-field guidance or reasons about the distilled section key set)_ _(e.g. Step 4's distill-seed.md edit made Out-of-scope/Deferred emit null (rendered from the concept tree instead) while keeping the 8-key _DISTILL_SECTION_KEYS shape and the distill tests green.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/create.py:create_plan runs its interactive operator gates in sequence (_review_step_change_types, then _review_step_gates), all reading the same yes / resume / input_fn context; a new interactive gate slots in after them reading that same context, and at that point the reviewed steps list and seed text are both in hand as evidence for a producer.** — The gate-sequencing convention and the shared yes/resume/input_fn plumbing mean a new gate reuses existing context rather than threading new params, and the post-review point is where the fully-reviewed step list is available. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds an interactive operator gate to create_plan)_ _(e.g. Step 4 added the concept gate as the third sequential gate after _review_step_gates, injecting prompt_fn=input_fn / yes=yes / a save_fn closure into navigate_concepts.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **create_plan's fail-loud placeholder check (_find_placeholder_body_sections, which rejects a body still containing _(TODO)_) is SKIPPED when budget.enabled (i.e. under --iterate); so any step that relies on that gate catching a section — or that must tolerate an empty section — must reason about both the --iterate (gate off) and non-iterate (gate on) paths, and a render-override step must land its overwrite before this check.** — The gate's on/off state flips with --iterate, so 'the TODO gate will catch this' only holds without --iterate; a step depending on either behavior must test both and place any body mutation upstream of the check. _(when: when a plan-tool step touches create's body sections and depends on (or must tolerate) the fail-loud TODO gate)_ _(e.g. Step 4 noted the overwrite must precede _find_placeholder_body_sections and added test_rendered_sections_are_not_todo (overriding the autouse TODO-disable fixture) to exercise the live gate on a tree-rendered body.)_
- `[cross-step]` **In create, the prospective plan path is output_dir / f'{slug}.md' (the exact value write_new_plan later uses) and is computable BEFORE the plan .md is written — so a concepts_path(plan_path) / grounding-style sidecar path inside plan-details/<slug>/ can be resolved (and its resume artifact read) during an early gate, before write_new_plan runs.** — Resolving the sidecar path only needs the plan path, and that path is deterministic from output_dir+slug at gate time, so a sidecar-backed resume/persist gate can run early without waiting for the plan file to exist. _(when: when a plan-tool step needs the plan path or a plan-details/<slug>/ sidecar path inside create before write_new_plan)_ _(e.g. Step 4 computed output_dir / f'{slug}.md' then concepts_path(plan_path), called read_concepts first for resume, and only emitted a fresh tree when none was saved.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/detail.py:generate_detail has TWO authoring paths — the serial `for step in serial_steps` loop AND `_generate_detail_concurrent` (taken when jobs > 1) — and already carries prompt_fn (default builtins.input) beside its invoker / lessons_invoker / foundational_invoker seams. A once-per-call post-authoring gate (e.g. the concept sign-off walk) must land in the serial tail AFTER `_generate_detail_concurrent` returns and before `results` is returned — never inside either loop or a concurrent worker — so single-step (inline) and full/batch (consolidated) runs both fall out of one placement.** — The concurrent path (jobs>1) is a distinct code path from the serial loop; a gate placed in the serial loop is skipped under jobs>1, and one placed in either loop/worker prompts N times and races on the single per-plan sidecar. The post-both-paths serial tail is the only spot that runs exactly once per call regardless of jobs or step_id. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a once-per-call post-authoring gate or a new seam to generate_detail, or reasons about its serial-vs-concurrent (jobs>1) authoring paths)_ _(e.g. Step 5 placed the concept walk after both the serial loop and _generate_detail_concurrent, just before generate_detail returns results; a new concept_invoker seam slots beside the existing invoker/lessons_invoker/foundational_invoker seams and prompt_fn is reused as the walk's prompt_fn.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/cli/authoring.py:cmd_detail's generate_detail(...) call currently passes NEITHER yes NOR prompt_fn (generate_detail defaults prompt_fn to builtins.input internally). A step that adds an interactive/unattended-sensitive gate to generate_detail must add both yes=args.yes and an interactive prompt_fn to that one call site — the args carry yes but it isn't wired through today.** — generate_detail's internal prompt_fn default keeps unit tests green, but the production cmd_detail path can neither honor -y nor reach the TTY for a new gate until this call is amended; an author trusting the internal default ships a gate that never runs interactively. _(when: when a plan-tool step needs cmd_detail to honor --yes or drive an interactive prompt through generate_detail)_ _(e.g. The cmd_detail call at authoring.py ~line 1214 passes step_id/force/dry_run/foundational_invoker/... but no yes= and no prompt_fn=; Step 5 identified this as the missing wiring for the concept walk's yes→non-TTY→interactive gate.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/review.py has TWO self-consistency producers that must return identical membership — collect_self_consistency_findings (read by the --iterate blocking signal) and _self_consistency_from_smells (feeds the finalize --fail-on-findings gate and the report), with parity pinned by TestCollectSelfConsistencyFindings. A new blocking-but-not-appliable check is folded into BOTH, and deliberately NOT into collect_deterministic_findings (that one feeds apply_finding's pre/post delta and is kept free of non-appliable findings by design/docstring).** — Adding the check to only one producer makes --iterate and the audit-only path disagree; adding it to collect_deterministic_findings routes a non-appliable finding into apply's delta. The three-way distinction is not obvious from the names. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a blocking deterministic completeness check to review.py)_ _(e.g. Step 6 wired check_concept_coverage into collect_self_consistency_findings AND _self_consistency_from_smells but not collect_deterministic_findings, mirroring orphaned-deliverable / suppression-shape.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/completeness_report.py:deferred_kind routes any non-apply-eligible, non-plan-completeness source to the 'diagnostic' kind by default, whose WHY text ('fix the declared path, run plan-tool detail') is wrong for most new sources. Giving a new deferred source a correct remedy requires FOUR coordinated edits: a special-case branch in deferred_kind, matching WHY and _HEADINGS entries, adding the kind to the by_kind disposition-summary counter, and adding it to the deferred-bucket 'for kind in (...)' loop in build_report_md.** — The default-to-diagnostic fall-through means a new source renders with a misleading remedy unless explicitly special-cased; the counter and the render loop are separate touchpoints, so missing either leaves the finding uncounted or unrendered even after deferred_kind is fixed. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a new non-apply-eligible finding source that should render a specific remedy in the curated completeness report)_ _(e.g. Step 6 special-cased concept-coverage to a concept-gate remedy across deferred_kind, WHY, _HEADINGS, the by_kind counter, and the deferred-bucket loop, while updating the '## Smells (advisory)' intro for the advisory concept-unsigned-deferral source.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/cli/completeness_apply_parallel.py:_capture_changes diffs ONLY the files in apply_finding's pre_snapshot (the plan .md plus every step that already had a detail file — see the NOTE at ~line 168), so any file outside that set — notably a plan-details/<slug>/ sidecar like concepts.json — is never captured into a FileChange and never replayed onto the canonical tree; a worker's write to such a sidecar is lost on teardown.** — The snapshot scope is the exact boundary of what parallel apply can persist; a design that assumes a worker can write a sidecar back is silently wrong, and the correct response is to make the value recompute-only rather than sidecar-persisted. _(when: when a plan-tool step reasons about what the parallel completeness-apply path can persist, or adds a sidecar under plan-details/<slug>/ that a worker might write)_ _(e.g. Step 6's no-loss regression pins that replay_results over an apply-eligible finding leaves a pre-existing concepts.json byte-unchanged and that _capture_changes emits no FileChange for it — the reason coverage is recomputed by slug, not stored.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **CLAUDE.md's Architecture section maintains one bold-lead paragraph per leaf/subsystem (e.g. **Granularity advisor (`granularity.py`)**, **Convergence diagnostic**, **Decision telemetry**, the Branch-awareness block). When a plan ships a NEW leaf module, its closing docs-reconciliation step must ADD a sibling-modeled Architecture paragraph naming the leaf, its command surface, its finding sources, and its key invariants — a missing paragraph reads as undocumented drift to the next reconcile audit.** — The Architecture section is the codebase's per-leaf registry; every other leaf has an entry, so an unregistered new leaf is the one gap the reconcile audit flags. Adding-a-paragraph is a distinct obligation from the step-7-style one-line touch-ups of EXISTING paragraphs. _(when: when a plan-tool step reconciles docs after shipping a new leaf/subsystem module)_ _(e.g. Step 9 added a **Concept sign-off gate (`concept_tree.py`)** paragraph modeled on the Granularity/Convergence/Telemetry/Branch-awareness siblings — naming the leaf, `scope-review`, the `concept-coverage`/`concept-unsigned-deferral` sources, the out-of-APPLY_ELIGIBLE_SOURCES + recompute-by-slug invariants.)_
- `[cross-step]` **For a plan-tool feature that both adds a new CLI command AND ships a new leaf, doc-registration ownership splits by step: CAPABILITIES.md, the generated docs/cli/ reference, and the --help golden are owned by the COMMAND-ADDING step (it registers the verb in the parser); the CLAUDE.md Architecture leaf paragraph, the RUNBOOK operator walkthrough, and the BACKLOG close are owned by the final docs-reconciliation step. The reconciliation step must NOT re-do the command-step's registration docs.** — docs/cli/ and the --help golden are drift-guarded against the argparse parser edited in the command step, so they land there naturally; pulling them into the later reconciliation step over-scopes it and double-owns a drift-guarded surface. Conversely the Architecture/RUNBOOK/BACKLOG surfaces aren't tied to the parser and belong in the reconciliation step. _(when: when a plan adds a new CLI command plus a new leaf and splits command-registration docs from a later docs-reconciliation step)_ _(e.g. Step 9 explicitly deferred registering `scope-review` in CAPABILITIES.md, docs/cli/, and the --help golden to step 8's registration work, and owned only the CLAUDE.md paragraph, RUNBOOK walkthrough, and #121 close.)_

- `[cross-step]` **plan_tool/run_log.py (the leaf) only has read_in_flight(path) — the LIVE in-progress snapshot reader; there is NO leaf-level reader for a COMPLETED run's JSONL events. The only completed-run readers, plan_tool/cli/runs.py:_iter_events and _load_events_with_skips, sit in the plan_tool.cli layer that cycle-free leaves (e.g. the telemetry resolver) cannot import. A leaf that needs a finished run's events must add its own leaf reader mirroring read_in_flight's Path-arg + degrade-on-error contract, not reach into cli/runs.py.** — An author who greps 'run-log reader' finds cli/runs.py and assumes reuse, but that import edge is forbidden from a leaf; the correct move is a new import-clean reader at run_log.py that returns [] / None on missing/garbage, tolerant like read_in_flight and telemetry.read_decisions. _(when: when a plan-tool leaf/telemetry step needs to read a completed run's JSONL events)_ _(e.g. Step 1 added read_run_events / read_run_outcome to run_log.py as the leaf twin of cli/runs.py:_iter_events, taking a Path like read_in_flight and returning []/None on any OSError.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/run_log.py:IterationEnd (event discriminator 'iteration_end') is a PHANTOM event: the dataclass is in the Event union but NO RunLogWriter method or any code anywhere constructs it (grep for `IterationEnd(` outside the class def returns nothing). A reader or consumer over run logs must tolerate zero iteration_end lines and must not assume the per-step outcome map is ever populated on real logs today.** — Specifying a reader as if iteration_end lines exist would leave the per-step branch untested against real data and could mislead a later step into thinking per-step run outcomes are already emitted; they are not — emitting IterationEnd is unwired work owned by a future step. _(when: when a plan-tool step reads or reasons about run-log iteration_end / IterationEnd events)_ _(e.g. read_run_outcome collects iteration_end lines into iteration_outcomes but the detail pins that this map is empty on every real log today (no producer), so the test uses synthetic lines and a no-iteration_end case.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **In plan_tool/run_log.py, RunLogWriter emit helpers (run_end, phase_start, iteration helpers, …) all merge caller kwargs via `**extra` into the serialized payload, so optional keys like run_end's `error` are present ONLY when the caller passed them — they are NOT guaranteed keys on the line. A reader must access them with .get('error') (default None), never index them directly.** — The `**extra` merge means the JSON line's key set is caller-dependent; a reader that assumes a fixed schema and subscripts `line['error']` will KeyError on the common case where no error was set. _(when: when a plan-tool step reads optional fields off a run_log.py event line)_ _(e.g. read_run_outcome copies outcome/rc/duration_ms off the run_end line but reads error via .get('error') → None, because run_end merges error through **extra only when supplied.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **In plan_tool/telemetry.py the `granularity` kind is OVERLOADED across ≥4 distinct decisions — record_granularity (decision 'assessed'), record_code_reveals_split ('code-reveals-split'), record_create_granularity_assessment ('create-review'), and create's ('create-step-outcome'). A telemetry consumer MUST disambiguate on the `(kind, decision)` pair, never `kind` alone.** — Matching a granularity consumer on kind alone conflates four unrelated decisions; only create-step-outcome is self-recording (result in context.action) while the other three are async — a kind-only match would mis-resolve or mis-bucket the async ones. The overload is invisible from the kind literal. _(when: when a plan-tool step reads, buckets, or resolves telemetry events whose kind is 'granularity')_ _(e.g. resolve_decision_inline matches `kind=='granularity' and decision==CREATE_DECISION_STEP_OUTCOME` for the inline family and returns None for 'assessed'/'code-reveals-split'/'create-review'; test_granularity_assessed_is_not_inline pins that split.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **The three self-recording plan-tool decision families record their result in a family-specific context key: apply-verdict→context['verdict'] (APPLIED/NOT-APPLICABLE/BLOCKED/BLOCKED-STRUCTURAL/UNKNOWN), escalate-split→context['outcome'] (applied/recommended/unsafe/proposal-unusable/step-missing), create-step-outcome→context['action'] (the CREATE_ACTION_* set). A consumer reads the result off that per-family key and should import the kind/action string constants FROM telemetry.py, not re-type the literals.** — These are the only in-call self-recording families (every other decision's outcome is async); knowing the exact result-key-per-family and the enumerated value sets lets a resolver map inline without a run-log join. Re-typing the literals lets telemetry_analysis and telemetry.py drift. _(when: when a plan-tool step consumes or resolves the outcome of apply-verdict, escalate-split, or create-step-outcome decision telemetry)_ _(e.g. telemetry_analysis imports APPLY_VERDICT_KIND / ESCALATE_SPLIT_KIND / CREATE_DECISION_STEP_OUTCOME / CREATE_ACTION_* from telemetry.py and reads context.get('verdict'/'outcome'/'action') defensively (str(...,'')) so a missing key resolves to still-open, never raises.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/convergence_diagnosis.py is the SOLE home of cross-run fingerprint/focus correlation in the codebase: reuse its matcher primitives _normalized_focus / _step_token / _matches / build_region_trends / RegionTrend and TITLE_SIMILARITY_CUTOFF (0.85). It is a cycle-free leaf that never imports back, so another leaf may import it at module top. Do NOT fold a new decision-level derivation into its _is_resolved_in_run — that helper is Annotation-keyed with a different verdict vocabulary; reuse the primitives, keep the derivation separate.** — An author who needs fuzzy/step/fingerprint matching will otherwise re-implement it or wrongly extend _is_resolved_in_run; the primitives are the reuse surface and the higher-level per-annotation verdict is not. _(when: when a plan-tool step needs cross-run fingerprint/focus/title matching or region-trend logic)_ _(e.g. Step 3's async resolver keys the decision's focus through _normalized_focus/_step_token and reads plan_fingerprint transitions via build_region_trends, adding no second matcher to telemetry_analysis.py.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/telemetry.py:DecisionEvent has NO step_id attribute — step_id folds into the decision_id hash only and is never stored on the event. A consumer that needs a decision's step focus must read it from context (e.g. code-reveals-split carries context['step_ids'], a PLURAL list) or parse it from event.anchor via convergence_diagnosis._step_token — never event.step_id.** — An author who assumes a symmetric step_id field (because it appears in the id-hash lesson and in create-side recorders) will write event.step_id and AttributeError; the stored focus signal lives in context/anchor and is plural for the split family. _(when: when a plan-tool step consumes a DecisionEvent's step focus for a join or bucketing)_ _(e.g. Step 3's focus derivation reads event.context.get('step_ids', []) for code-reveals-split, else a step<N> token from event.anchor via _step_token, else the fuzzy-title path.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/run_log.py:run_log_path(repo_root, slug, run_id) is the leaf-accessible builder for a completed run's JSONL path that step-1's read_run_outcome reads; a telemetry/resolver joining on DecisionEvent.run_id pairs run_log_path + read_run_outcome, treating run_id == '' as the 'no run anchor' skip (authoring-time/create decisions carry run_id='') and read_run_outcome's None (missing log) vs RunOutcome.completed=False (crashed/in-flight) as distinct join signals.** — The run-log join needs the path builder and the reader together, and the empty-run_id / None / completed=False trichotomy is the difference between 'skip this source', 'no run', and 'still-open' — collapsing any two mis-resolves the verdict. _(when: when a plan-tool leaf/telemetry step joins a decision to a completed run's outcome)_ _(e.g. resolve_decisions builds run_log_path(repo_root, event.plan_slug, event.run_id) only when run_id is non-empty, then read_run_outcome; completed=False leans still-open, None skips the run source.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **The plan_tool/telemetry_analysis.py leaf's module-top plan_tool import allowlist widens beyond {telemetry} to the read-only sibling leaves it joins across — run_log, convergence_diagnosis, review_persistence, locator — all cycle-free leaves that never import back, so they sit at module top; plan_tool.cli stays forbidden and the boundary test must still pass with the wider set. Slug→plan-path resolution routes through locator's manifest listing and degrades to no-history on a miss (deleted/renamed plan, plan_slug=='').** — A future reconcile audit could read the widened imports as boundary drift; documenting that these four are the intended, cycle-safe additions (and cli remains the one forbidden edge) keeps the boundary test's expected set current, and the tolerant slug resolution is what keeps the ownerless/renamed tail counted-but-uncorrelated rather than crashing. _(when: when a plan-tool step widens a cycle-free leaf's cross-leaf import set or resolves a plan_slug to a plan path from a leaf)_ _(e.g. Step 3 added module-top imports for run_log/convergence_diagnosis/review_persistence/locator and kept test_telemetry_analysis_does_not_import_cli green; a slug absent from the manifest resolves to history=None and the sidecar source is simply skipped.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **Registering a new plan-tool subcommand requires FIVE coordinated touchpoints beyond the new plan_tool/cli/<name>_cmd.py (cmd_* handler + register(subparsers)): (a) app.py — the two-line import pair (`from plan_tool.cli import <name>_cmd as _<name>_commands` + the cmd_* name) AND adding _<name>_commands to the COMMAND_MODULES tuple; (b) parser.py — add the command literal to CANONICAL_COMMAND_ORDER (absent → it sorts last in --help); (c) CAPABILITIES.md — an owning capability listing the subcommand in `surfaces:` or capability_catalog.check_capabilities flags it `orphan-subcommand`, using only real MISSION principle ids; (d) regenerate docs/cli/<name>.md via `python -m plan_tool.cli_reference --write` (drift-guarded by tests/cli/test_cli_reference.py — never hand-author); (e) re-baseline the --help golden if one covers per-command help.** — COMMAND_MODULES is the dispatch table and CANONICAL_COMMAND_ORDER is the independent help-ordering list — placement in one does not imply the other. The orphan-subcommand honesty check and the byte-compared generated doc both fail the build if omitted, and neither is visible from the handler module. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a new CLI subcommand)_ _(e.g. Step 5 wired telemetry_cmd.py into COMMAND_MODULES (app.py) + CANONICAL_COMMAND_ORDER (parser.py), added a decision-telemetry capability to CAPABILITIES.md (which also gave the recorder leaf plan_tool/telemetry.py its first catalog home), and regenerated docs/cli/telemetry.md.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **A repo-wide plan-tool analysis command mirrors plan_tool/cli/convergence_cmd.py's cmd_*/register(subparsers) shape but takes NO positional plan-name argument and does NOT call resolve_plan_for_context — it loads context and passes ctx.repo_root straight through, exactly like plan_tool/cli/inspect.py:cmd_list. convergence is per-plan (resolves one plan); telemetry/list aggregate across all plans.** — convergence_cmd is the natural template for a read-only, no-Claude, no-run-log, always-exit-0 analysis surface, but copying it wholesale would wrongly add a `name` positional and a per-plan resolve to a command whose whole point is cross-plan aggregation; cmd_list is the correct template for the repo-wide half. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a read-only analysis command that aggregates across all plans rather than focusing one plan)_ _(e.g. Step 5's cmd_telemetry copied convergence_cmd's module docstring/contract and register() shape but dropped the name arg, calling analyze_decisions(ctx.repo_root) with no plan resolution — mirroring cmd_list.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool concept publication currently has three distinct authorities: concept_sync.synchronize_concepts owns compare-and-swap plus atomic publication, detail.generate_detail saves concept changes only after successful detail writes, and scope_out.apply_narrow owns archive/rename journaling plus restoration.** — These flows may share pure preparation, but treating their publication sequences as interchangeable would change failure and rollback behavior before the later transaction steps land. _(when: when a plan refactors or unifies concept changes across synchronization, detail authoring, and scope-out)_ _(e.g. Step 1 should centralize candidate construction in concept_sync.py while retaining each caller’s existing publication tail.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **Detail deferral replacement is an ordered whole-step operation: include only successfully written details, remove every affected step’s old links before adding replacements, preserve unrelated metadata, encode retained step IDs as a compact JSON list, delete the metadata key when empty, and save one candidate in deterministic step order.** — Changing any part of this sequence can retain obsolete links, erase unrelated metadata, persist an empty pseudo-link, or make concurrent authoring nondeterministic. _(when: when a plan changes plan_tool detail_deferral_step_ids preparation or concurrent detail-side concept updates)_ _(e.g. The behavior currently owned by detail.py:_replace_detail_deferrals should move intact into concept_sync.py rather than be re-derived from final results.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **Scope-out concept preparation changes only concepts that lose their final committed owner, delegates signed decision metadata to concept_review.review_concept_scope(sign_off=True), and must preserve the original sidecar text/state needed by apply_narrow’s stale checks and rollback.** — A carved concept may still have a surviving owner, and the prepared candidate alone is insufficient to verify or restore the publication precondition. _(when: when a plan modifies scope-out concept-tree preparation or moves it into a shared concept module)_ _(e.g. scope_out.py may delegate copying and ownerless deferral mutation to concept_sync.py, but must retain loading, ownership checks, original-state capture, journaling, and restoration.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **concept_sync synchronization fingerprints the fully rendered candidate plan bytes together with the existing ordered detail files, then stores that fingerprint on the candidate ConceptTree before validation and serialization.** — Hashing the source plan, unordered details, or a post-serialization variant would create a sidecar fingerprint that does not identify the exact publication candidate. _(when: when a plan refactors synchronized concept candidate construction or fingerprint assignment)_ _(e.g. Preserve concept_sync.py:_fingerprint framing when extracting synchronize_concepts candidate construction.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **The concept-scope erasure mechanism is: concept_sync.py:render_scope_decisions renders only nodes with review_state == 'approved', so an all-unsigned tree yields empty bodies for both owned sections and parser.py:replace_body_sections then replaces each matched section with a bare newline — erasing existing '## Deferred'/'## Out of scope' prose. The signed/unsigned predicate is ANY approved node (create.py's signed_concept_scope, ~line 6236): a mixed tree with one approved node takes the full signed path, where the record is the authority and unreviewed nodes simply render nothing.** — This mechanism is why create.py's unsigned arms historically bypassed the synchronizer with direct save_concepts calls; any step touching signed/unsigned concept routing must know the predicate is any-approved (not all-approved) and that erasure comes from the render+replace pair, not from save logic. _(when: when a plan-tool step reasons about signed vs unsigned concept trees in concept_sync.py or create.py's concept routing)_ _(e.g. Step 1's whole-tree gate computes the predicate from reviewed_tree; test_mixed_tree_takes_signed_path pins that one approved defer plus one unreviewed node still re-renders the owned sections.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **concept_sync.py's publication tail has two semantics to preserve: refresh_plan_provenance records the plan text the tool left on disk (called with final_plan_text on the success tail and with current_plan_text after a rollback restore), so an arm that never publishes plan text must SKIP it entirely — existing provenance stays valid; and _restore(path, old_text, publish) unlinks the file when old_text is None, so a publication-failure rollback for a sidecar that did not previously exist must pass None and assert no file is left behind.** — Calling refresh_plan_provenance from a no-plan-write arm would record a publication that never happened, and a rollback that writes an empty file instead of unlinking leaves a phantom sidecar that the next sync's divergence check would trip over. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds or modifies a publication/rollback arm in concept_sync.py)_ _(e.g. The unsigned arm skips refresh_plan_provenance and reuses _restore with current_sidecar_text; test_unsigned_sidecar_publication_failure_without_prior_sidecar_leaves_none pins the unlink case.)_
- `[cross-step]` **concept_sync.py:_fingerprint(plan_path, staged_bytes) applies review_persistence.compute_plan_fingerprint's exact framing (plan bytes, then each plan-details/<slug>/*.md as name\0content sorted by name), so when the staged bytes equal the on-disk plan bytes the result equals compute_plan_fingerprint(plan_path) — this equality is the load-bearing bridge that makes routing the direct save_concepts+compute_plan_fingerprint call sites (create.py's two unsigned fallbacks, detail.py's deferral persistence, scope_out.py's apply_narrow) through synchronize_concepts behavior-preserving.** — An author changing either helper's framing, or an unsigned-arm implementation that fingerprints anything other than current on-disk bytes, silently breaks the equivalence steps 3–5 rest on; the pinned equality test in test_concept_sync.py is the only guard. _(when: when a plan-tool step touches concept_sync._fingerprint, compute_plan_fingerprint framing, or routes a direct save_concepts caller through synchronize_concepts)_ _(e.g. The unsigned arm computes _fingerprint(path, current_plan_text.encode('utf-8')) and the detail pins its equality with compute_plan_fingerprint(path) in a dedicated test cited by step 3.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **create_plan's collision-replace failure window runs from the first archive_existing_source call to append_to_manifest returning, and the failure sites inside it are: write_new_plan, the post-write reparse CreateError, the signed synchronize_concepts rejection (which ALREADY unlinks the new plan and its concepts sidecar before raising — cleanup layers must tolerate absence), the unsigned save_concepts, and append_to_manifest itself; remove_from_manifest has already committed its removal to disk at window-open, so the removed repo-relative strings are the manifest re-add work list.** — A recovery design that misses the window boundaries either double-unlinks against the pre-cleaned sync arm, forgets the manifest re-add (removal is immediate, not deferred), or extends restore past the commit and destroys a validly registered plan. _(when: when a plan-tool step touches create_plan's should_replace/collision-archive region or adds failure handling around it)_ _(e.g. Step 2's handler wraps exactly the should_replace loop through append_to_manifest, suppresses FileNotFoundError on the predicted-plan and concepts_path unlinks, and re-adds each replaced_manifest_entries item via append_to_manifest.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/create.py:archive_existing_source returns ArchiveResult.archived as (original, archived) Path pairs — the plan-source pair first, then one pair per detail-bundle FILE (directories never listed), with numbered .replaced.N targets already resolved — and _replacement_notice (a two-line blockquote ending in a blank line, parameterized only by pathutil.display_path(predicted, repo_root) — renamed from a create-local _display_path on 2026-08-02) is prepended only to .md files; non-.md detail files are byte-copied with no notice.** — An inverse or auditor of the archive can work purely from the pair list with no target arithmetic of its own, but must branch on the .md suffix for notice handling — assuming every file carries the notice, or that directories appear in the pair list, produces a wrong restore. _(when: when a plan-tool step consumes archive_existing_source's ArchiveResult or reasons about the archived-collision on-disk shape)_ _(e.g. restore_archived_collisions iterates the pairs directly, strips the exact notice from .md files only, and prunes the emptied archived detail directory afterward.)_
- `[cross-step]` **The archive-before-validate shape has three distinct plan-tool sites with different recovery ownership: create_plan's collision archive (this step's restore), plan_tool/detail.py:_archive_existing_detail (detail replacement — same shape, separately owned), and the CLI-side seed archive, which runs only AFTER create_plan returns successfully and therefore can never strand anything and needs no restore window.** — A grep for the archive shape surfaces all three sites; without the ownership split an author either over-scopes a create-side fix into detail.py or wrongly wraps the post-success seed archive in recovery machinery it cannot need. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds restore/recovery around an archive-existing-artifact call site or audits which archive sites need one)_ _(e.g. Step 2's Deferred routes _archive_existing_detail to step 6, and its shared-logic check pins that the TestCliArchivesOriginalSeed flow sits outside the failure window.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **create_plan has exactly two unsigned concept-persistence sites, each with a signed sibling in the same branch that is its call-shape template: the else arm below signed_concept_scope (post-write; no sidecar exists on disk there because archive_existing_source moved any colliding/resumed bundle before write_new_plan, so original_tree=None) and the elif budget.enabled arm before return CreateResult (iterate tail; after append_to_manifest, so a failure must leave the registered plan intact). The unsigned arms skip the signed arm's post-sync reparse because they never touch the plan file.** — Mirroring the adjacent signed call is the low-risk routing shape, the two sites straddle the manifest commit so their failure tails must differ, and original_tree=None at the post-write site is a flow invariant of the archive-before-write sequence, not an assumption. _(when: when a plan-tool step touches create_plan's unsigned concept persistence or routes concept-sidecar writes inside create)_ _(e.g. Step 3's post-write call is synchronize_concepts(plan_path, parsed_written_plan, None, concept_tree, source_plan_text=...) with the signed arm's suppress-FileNotFoundError cleanup on failure; the iterate-tail call mirrors the signed budget.enabled arm and raises CreateError without unlinks.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/concept_tree.py:save_concepts serializes exactly json.dumps(asdict(tree), indent=2, allow_nan=False) + '\n' — the same bytes synchronize_concepts builds for both its expected_sidecar compare-and-swap value and its published sidecar — so an unmutated in-memory ConceptTree can serve as original_tree against a sidecar a previous sync call wrote.** — create's iterate-tail sync passes the in-memory tree as original_tree and relies on this byte equality for its compare-and-swap; changing either serializer's framing breaks the equality and turns every iterate-tail sync into a false SOURCE_DIVERGENCE. _(when: when a plan-tool step changes concept sidecar serialization or passes an in-memory tree as synchronize_concepts's original_tree)_ _(e.g. The signed budget.enabled arm already rested on this equality; step 3's unsigned iterate-tail call reuses the reasoning verbatim and cites it in its Input section.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **A ConceptTree entering synchronize_concepts must carry a non-empty concept fingerprint to pass _validate_tree — create's trees get it from the concept_fingerprint hash set near bootstrap_concepts — so a routing step deletes only the caller-side plan_fingerprint computation (the sync owns that), never the bootstrap concept_fingerprint the caller still supplies.** — The two fingerprints look interchangeable at the call site; deleting the wrong one makes the sync's validation reject every tree, while leaving the plan_fingerprint computation in place defeats the point of routing through the sync. _(when: when a plan-tool step constructs or routes a ConceptTree into synchronize_concepts and must decide which fingerprint the caller still owns)_ _(e.g. Step 3's 'parts that must not vary' pins that concept_tree still carries its existing non-empty bootstrap fingerprint into both synchronize_concepts calls while both compute_plan_fingerprint computations in the fallback arms are deleted.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **At generate_detail's tail, the plan parsed at the top of the run is STALE — every successful step's update_step_detail_field round-tripped the plan through parse_plan/write_plan (and an auto-split may have renumbered), so tail consumers of plan state must re-parse from disk (the auto-split arm's final_plan is the in-file precedent); the concept tree loaded at the top is safe to reuse as-is, because generate_detail never mutates it (_replace_detail_deferrals deep-copies), making it a valid original_tree/compare-and-swap baseline.** — The two top-of-run artifacts age differently across the run — the plan goes stale per step while the tree stays byte-faithful to the sidecar — and knowing which is which is what makes a tail-of-run persistence call correct without re-loading everything. _(when: when a plan-tool step consumes plan or concept-tree state at the tail of generate_detail, or adds a persistence/gate call after the authoring loops)_ _(e.g. Step 4's routed call is synchronize_concepts(plan_path, fresh_plan_parsed_at_tail, concept_tree_loaded_at_top, reviewed_tree); passing the top-of-run plan would drop detail: pointers, and passing anything but the unmutated loaded tree would break the sidecar compare-and-swap.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/detail.py deliberately imports cross-module seams at MODULE TOP so tests can monkeypatch them as plan_tool.detail.<symbol> — apply_finding is the commented precedent and synchronize_concepts joins it; the detail→concept_sync edge is cycle-safe because concept_sync.py imports only concept_tree, parser, and schema, none of which import detail. Do not make these function-local: detail.py is an orchestrator, not an import-clean leaf, and the leaf convention does not apply to it.** — The codebase has two opposite import conventions — function-local for stdlib-only leaves, module-top-for-patchability in orchestrators — and applying the leaf rule to detail.py would break every test that patches plan_tool.detail.<seam>. _(when: when a plan-tool step adds a cross-module seam to plan_tool/detail.py (or another orchestrator) that tests must patch or spy on)_ _(e.g. Step 4 imports replace_detail_deferrals and synchronize_concepts at detail.py's module top, citing the existing apply_finding patchability comment; the re-targeted spy test patches plan_tool.detail.synchronize_concepts.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **A plan whose file was last written by parser.py:write_plan re-renders with byte-identical frontmatter through concept_sync's signed path, because render_plan_text and write_plan share the same yaml.safe_dump serialization of model_dump(exclude_defaults=True, exclude_none=True) — so a mid-flow signed sync after update_step_detail_field writes is frontmatter-byte-stable, unlike the hand-written-plan case where the parse→render round-trip normalizes bytes.** — The earlier captured lesson ('leave untouched is stronger than write unchanged') warns that re-render can change bytes; this is the precise counterpart condition under which re-render is safe, and it is what lets detail's tail route through the signed arm without a byte-preservation carve-out. _(when: when a plan-tool step reasons about whether concept_sync's signed republish (or any render_plan_text round-trip) changes plan bytes, and must decide if a preserve carve-out is needed)_ _(e.g. Step 4's signed-tree arm republishes the plan via render_plan_text with no byte-drift concern because generate_detail's own update_step_detail_field calls guarantee write_plan was the last writer.)_
- `[cross-step]` **After step 4, the detail_deferral_step_ids metadata key has one writer (concept_sync's public replacement helper, called from generate_detail's tail) and three readers: the public reader in concept_sync consumed by detail.py's _format_concept_scope_block (prompt rendering) and _included_deferral_step_ids (include-transition regen gate), plus plan_tool/review.py:_structured_concept_deferral_is_valid, which still parses the raw key independently with its own validation — consolidating review.py onto the public reader is a reconcile-owned follow-up, not owned by any plan step.** — A future plan touching deferral-link validation will grep the key, find two parse implementations, and needs to know the split is deliberate-but-temporary (reconcile-owned) rather than accidental duplication to fix in-step, which would over-scope into review.py. _(when: when a plan-tool step reads, validates, or consolidates the detail_deferral_step_ids source_metadata key)_ _(e.g. Step 4's Shared-logic note and Deferred list pin exactly this reader map and route the review.py consolidation to reconcile.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/scope_out.py:NarrowPreview.renumber is the old→new step-id map (ids absent from it are unchanged survivors; preview.carved_ids are the dropped ids), and concept nodes' source_metadata['step_id'] values use pre-narrow numbering until explicitly remapped — _prepare_concept_narrow_update is the place to rewrite them (candidate tree only; carved owners pop the key, the same ownerless shape create uses; _mapped_scopes skips keyless nodes while render_scope_decisions still renders the deferral).** — Narrow renumbering keeps ids contiguous, so an unremapped mapping points at a different surviving step and concept_sync's _mapped_scopes silently applies the scope to the wrong step (or refuses with MAPPING_CONFLICT on a dangling id) — the remap is mandatory correctness for any sync after a narrow, and original_tree must keep pre-narrow ids for the sidecar compare-and-swap. _(when: when a plan-tool step renumbers plan steps while a concepts.json sidecar carries source_metadata step_id mappings, or touches _prepare_concept_narrow_update / _mapped_scopes)_ _(e.g. Step 5's remap in _prepare_concept_narrow_update: carved id → pop('step_id'), renumbered id → str(new id), anything else left as-is; pinned by test_scope_out_drops_step_id_for_carved_concepts and test_original_tree_keeps_prenarrow_step_ids.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **apply_narrow's routed synchronize_concepts call has a fixed shape: plan_snapshot=preview.narrowed_plan (byte-stable because write_plan just serialized that exact object), source_plan_text left at default (apply_narrow legitimately rewrote the plan; the sidecar compare-and-swap plus apply_narrow's own pre-move checks are the real guards), non-success results converted to NarrowError inside the journaled try, and on PUBLICATION_FAILURE the sync has already self-rolled-back so the except arm's sidecar restore is a redundant-but-harmless backstop.** — Each element is load-bearing: a pre-narrow source_plan_text refuses on every run, a stale snapshot re-renders wrong frontmatter, a missed status→NarrowError conversion silently commits a refused publication, and not knowing the sync self-rolls-back tempts either double-restore bugs or deletion of the journal replay. _(when: when a plan-tool step touches apply_narrow's concept-persistence tail or its rollback interplay with synchronize_concepts)_ _(e.g. Step 5's concept tail in apply_narrow after write_plan; test_sync_refusal_rolls_back_narrow patches plan_tool.concept_sync.synchronize_concepts to return SOURCE_DIVERGENCE and asserts NarrowError plus full restore.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **Scope-out has three concept dispositions and two are asymmetric invariants: it must NEVER create a sidecar (the concept_update-is-None short-circuit when there is no record and no carved concept_ids is load-bearing), and any scope-out that defers a carved ownerless concept necessarily takes the SIGNED sync arm — concept_review.review_concept_scope(sign_off=True) sets review_state='approved' — so the deferral renders into the narrowed plan's ## Deferred section (a deliberate behavior change vs the historical direct save_concepts write, which left prose stale).** — An author reasoning 'scope-out is unsigned-ish, sidecar-only' picks the wrong arm: the fresh sign-off flips the whole-tree any-approved predicate, so the plan file IS republished and hand-written Deferred/Out-of-scope prose is replaced by the record's rendering — this must be tested as intended behavior, not flagged as a regression. _(when: when a plan-tool step reasons about which concept_sync arm a scope-out takes or whether scope-out can create concepts.json)_ _(e.g. test_scope_out_without_concept_record_creates_no_sidecar and test_signed_scope_out_renders_carved_deferral_into_deferred_section pin the two ends.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **After the concept-write-integrity plan, the repo invariant 'no concepts.json writer outside concept_sync.py' is pinned by tests/test_concept_sync.py's token-scan guard (save_concepts/write_concepts allowed only in concept_tree.py and concept_sync.py); a future step that needs to persist concept state must route through synchronize_concepts, never extend the allowlist or add a direct save_concepts call.** — The allowlist encodes the designed single-writer boundary, and extending it re-opens the record/prose divergence and fingerprint-staleness gaps three steps of routing just closed; the plain text scan also rejects comments naming the removed writers. _(when: when a plan-tool step needs to write or persist concepts.json, or trips the sidecar-writer guard test)_ _(e.g. test_no_concept_sidecar_writer_outside_concept_sync rglobs plan_tool/**/*.py from plan_tool.__file__ and asserts the token allowlist.)_
- `[cross-step]` **Two staleness facts around narrows are deliberate, not bugs to fix in a routing step: detail_deferral_step_ids links go stale when a narrow renumbers steps (a pre-existing gap the routed sync does not validate — BACKLOG-owned, needs its own carved-vs-surviving link-semantics decision), and signoff_source_state deliberately keeps the pre-narrow fingerprint the decision was made against (it records provenance, not currency — renormalizing it after a narrow would erase what the sign-off was bound to).** — A future plan grepping for stale-after-renumber state will find both and must know one is deferred work with an open design question and the other is intentionally never refreshed — 'fixing' either inside a scope-out step over-scopes it or destroys provenance. _(when: when a plan-tool step encounters pre-narrow step ids or fingerprints persisted in concepts.json after a scope-out)_ _(e.g. Step 5's Deferred routes the detail_deferral_step_ids remap to BACKLOG.md and pins 'renormalizing signoff_source_state would erase that provenance'.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/detail.py:_author_step_detail is the single shared per-step authoring unit for BOTH the serial loop and _generate_detail_concurrent — a per-step change to gating, writing, or outcome shape lands once there and covers serial and jobs>1 alike (contrast once-per-call gates, which belong in the tail after both paths). Its failed-write outcome contract is frozen: succeeded=False, written=False, skipped_reason starting 'write failed: ', handle.fail(...), phase_outcome='error' — consumed by run-log tests and test_concurrent_write_oserror_isolated.** — Knowing the shared unit avoids duplicating a fix across the two authoring paths or wrongly placing it in one loop; and the failure-reporting strings are load-bearing test keys, so a fix must change what's on disk after a failure, never how the failure is reported. _(when: when a plan-tool step changes per-step detail authoring/write behavior or its failure reporting in detail.py)_ _(e.g. Step 6's temp-write/restore rework edits only _author_step_detail's write block and automatically covers jobs>1; all three retargeted write-failure tests keep their original assertions on the frozen contract.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/detail.py:_archive_existing_detail is best-effort: it returns the archive destination Path on success and None BOTH when there was nothing to archive AND when the move failed — so a non-None return is exactly the 'restore is possible and may be needed' discriminator, and a None return with a pre-existing file at the canonical path is the truncate-in-place hole. Its archive message wording is pinned by test_archived_previous_detail_plain and must not change.** — A recovery design that treats None as 'nothing was there' silently misses the failed-move case; the return-value semantics are the entire basis for deciding when a restore arm fires. _(when: when a plan-tool step consumes _archive_existing_detail's return value or adds recovery around detail replacement)_ _(e.g. Step 6's restore arm fires only when _archive_existing_detail returned non-None and something raised afterward; the None-with-prior-file case is closed by the temp-write, not by restore.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **plan-details/<slug>/ is a pattern-sensitive directory: files matching *.md there are consumed by _archive_orphan_details ({step_id:02d}-*.md), _discover_siblings plus the concurrent sibling snapshot (*.md), and review_persistence.compute_plan_fingerprint's framing — so any non-detail file matching *.md leaks into sibling prompts and silently perturbs the plan fingerprint that concept-sync compare-and-swaps key on. Scratch/temp files written there must not end in .md.** — The glob consumers are spread across three modules and none errors on an unexpected match — a stray .md file corrupts prompts and fingerprints with no visible failure, breaking the step-4 routed sync's compare-and-swap downstream. _(when: when a plan-tool step writes any extra file into a plan-details/<slug>/ directory)_ _(e.g. Step 6's temp name uses prefix f'.{output_path.stem}.' and suffix '.tmp' specifically to miss all three glob surfaces; the fingerprint-stability test pins it.)_
- `[cross-step]` **detail.py's four _archive_existing_detail-shaped archive sites split by recovery need: only _author_step_detail's displaces the ACTIVE detail file before success and needs a restore window; _migrate_downstream_details_after_split and _migrate_downstream_details_after_merge archive an orphan already sitting at a rename destination (the active old_path is untouched — no window), and merge_steps' tail archives folded files only after the merged step's re-author succeeded (post-success — nothing strandable). Don't wrap the other three in recovery machinery.** — A grep for archive calls in detail.py surfaces all four; without the active-vs-orphan and pre-vs-post-success classification an author over-scopes recovery onto sites that cannot strand anything. _(when: when a plan-tool step audits detail.py archive call sites for stranded-artifact or restore-window work)_ _(e.g. Step 6's Deferred section pins exactly this taxonomy and leaves the split/merge migration archives and the merge_steps tail as-is.)_
- `[domain-shape]` **In _author_step_detail, save_checkpoint persists the parsed raw response BEFORE the write block, and the caller discards the checkpoint only after the plan's detail pointer is set — so a failed detail write never loses the REPLACEMENT body (it is recoverable on the next run); a write-failure fix therefore only needs to protect the PRIOR body, and together the two guarantees mean a failed replacement loses nothing.** — Without knowing the checkpoint ordering an author might over-engineer replacement-body recovery into the write path, or wrongly conclude a failed write loses the authored response. _(when: when a plan-tool step reasons about what is lost or recoverable on a detail write failure)_ _(e.g. Step 6's Input section cites the checkpoint call above the write block as the reason the fix scope is prior-body-only.)_

- `[detail-authoring]` **tests/test_data_contract.py is a section-scoped drift guard over DATA_CONTRACT.md: each test keys documented field rows in one section against the runtime dataclasses (e.g. test_concept_contract_is_documented requires 'concepts.json' to appear in the Concept sidecar section). Pure prose added inside an existing section is guard-safe; new field-shaped table rows or new top-level sections are what trip it. Invariant documentation belongs as prose in the owning existing section, followed by running that suite.** — The guard's granularity (per-section field keys, not byte comparison) is not documented in DATA_CONTRACT.md itself; knowing prose-is-safe / rows-are-not lets a docs step land contract commentary without reverse-engineering the test. _(when: when a plan-tool step edits DATA_CONTRACT.md or documents a persisted-schema invariant)_ _(e.g. Step 8 added the concepts.json single-writer invariant as prose extending the '## Concept sidecar' section's existing 'Saves validate … atomically replace' sentence, with 'uv run pytest tests/test_data_contract.py -q' as acceptance.)_
- `[cross-step]` **When DATA_CONTRACT.md prose cites a guard test or symbol by name (e.g. the concepts.json single-writer token-scan test in tests/test_concept_sync.py), the citing step must copy the exact name from the test file at HEAD and pin its existence via the cited suite in acceptance — never transcribe the name from the plan's own detail files, which may predate a rename during implementation.** — Plan details are authored before their dependency steps run; a test named in a step-5 detail can land under a different name, and DATA_CONTRACT.md has no drift guard over cited test names, so a stale citation survives silently. _(when: when a plan-tool docs step cites test or symbol names that were created by earlier steps in the same plan)_ _(e.g. Step 8's 'parts that must not vary' pins 'every symbol and test name cited in the new prose is copied from HEAD, not from this plan's details', with tests/test_concept_sync.py -q in acceptance to prove the cited guard exists.)_

- `[domain-shape]` **plan_tool/concept_tree.py:emit_concept_tree (the speculative sub-concept enrichment) has exactly ONE app-wide caller — create_plan's no-saved-tree branch (~create.py:5956); plan_tool/cli/scope_review_cmd.py already derives its tree from bootstrap_concepts + rederive_concepts WITHOUT enrichment and tolerates an absent record, so a bootstrap-only (section-node-only) concepts.json is an established valid record shape, not a degraded one.** — A future step touching concept enrichment/materialization needs to know the enrichment call is single-sited (contained blast radius) and that scope-review is the precedent proving non-enriched trees are already a supported shape — so 'thin bootstrap' or 'record-absent' don't need new plumbing. _(when: when a plan-tool step reasons about concept-tree enrichment, materialization, or whether a thin/absent concepts.json is valid)_ _(e.g. Step 1 removed the single emit_concept_tree caller and used the bootstrap tree directly, citing scope-review's derive path as the precedent that a bootstrap-only record is valid.)_
